en: A young dog, especially before sexual maturity (12–18 months).
A young rat.
To bring forth whelps or give birth to pups.

puppy.ety:
From earlier puppie (“a woman's pet dog”), of uncertain origin, but probably from Middle English *puppee, *poupee, from Old French poupée, popée (“a doll; puppet”). More at puppet.
Mostly displaced native Middle English whelp (“puppy”), from Old English hwelp, whence Modern English whelp and whelpie.

ex.en: Mary was the one who named this puppy.
ex.ja: この子犬の名付け親は、メアリーです。

ex.en: The puppy grew larger and larger every day.
ex.ja: 子犬は日に日に大きくなった。

ex.en: I've been searching for my puppy for weeks.
ex.ja: 僕は何週間も前からうちの子犬をさがしているんだ。

note.ja: フランス語 poupée（人形）から。「かわいい小さなもの」→「子犬」。puppet（あやつり人形）と同じ語源。

en: The process or art of finding candidates for a post in an organization, or recruits for the armed forces.
A style or process of recruiting.

note.ja: recruit（募集する）+ -ment。フランス語 recroître（再び育つ）から。「軍に新しく育ってくる兵」→「新兵・新人を募集すること」。

en: A nonmetallic element (symbol Si) with an atomic number of 14 and atomic weight of 28.0855.
A single atom of this element.

silicon.ety:

Coined by Scottish chemist Thomas Thomson as a modification of the earlier name silicium, from the stem of Latin silex (“flint, silica”) + -on from carbon.

ex.en: Powders of aluminium, magnesium, silicon, etc. explode.
ex.ja: アルミニウム、マグネシウム、シリコンなどの粉末が爆発する。

note.ja: ラテン語 silex（火打ち石）から。火打ち石に多く含まれる元素 →「ケイ素」。silicone（樹脂のシリコーン）とは別物。

en: That which is thin and broad.
A thin, broad piece cut off.
To cut into slices.
To cut with an edge using a drawing motion.
Having the properties of a slice knot.

slice.ety: From Middle English sclise, sklise, from Old French esclice, esclis (“a piece split off”), deverbal of esclicer, esclicier (“to splinter, split up”), from Frankish *slitjan (“to split up”), from Proto-Germanic *slitjaną, from Proto-Germanic *slītaną (“to split, tear apart”), from Proto-Indo-European *sleyd- (“to rend, injure, crumble”). Akin to Old High German sliz, gisliz (“a tear, rip”), Old High German slīȥan (“to tear”), Old English slītan (“to split up”), modern French éclisse. More at slite, slit.

ex.en: How many slices of pizza did you eat?
ex.ja: ピザ何切れ食べた？

ex.en: How many slices of meat would you like?
ex.ja: 肉は何切れにしましょうか。

ex.en: My mother is slicing the cake into eight pieces.
ex.ja: ケーキは、母さんが8つに切り分けてくれてるよ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 esclice（木片）から。「薄く割ったもの」→「薄切り・一切れ」。

en: A rigid implement, often roughly y-shaped, that is fixed to one's heel for the purpose of prodding a horse. Often worn by, and emblematic…
A jab given with the spurs.
To prod (especially a horse) on the side or flank, with the intent to urge motion or haste, to gig.
To urge or encourage to action, or to a more vigorous pursuit of an object

spur.ety: From Middle English spure, spore, from Old English spora, spura, from Proto-West Germanic *spurō, from Proto-Germanic *spurô, from Proto-Indo-European *sperH- (“to kick”).

ex.en: More money for education will spur economic growth.
ex.ja: 教育にもっとお金をかければ、経済成長に拍車がかかるだろう。

ex.en: Her desire to be a doctor spurred her on.
ex.ja: 彼女の医者になりたいと言う欲求が彼女を駆り立てた。

ex.en: What on earth spurred them to such an action?
ex.ja: 一体何が彼らをそのような行動に駆り立てたのか？

note.ja: 古英語 spura（拍車）から。spurn（はねつける）と同系。「馬の腹を突く金具」→「刺激・駆り立てる」。on the spur of the moment（とっさに）。

en: A person who subscribes to a publication or a service.
A system or component that subscribes to something, such as an event, made available by a publisher.

ex.en: How many subscribers does this magazine have?
ex.ja: この雑誌の発行部数はどのくらいですか。

note.ja: sub（下に）+ scrib（書く）+ er。（書類の）下に名前を書いた人 →「加入者・定期購読者」。

en: Synonym of telegraphy, any process for transmitting arbitrarily long messages over a long distance using a symbolic code.
The electrical device gradually developed in the early 19th century to transmit messages (telegrams) using Morse code; the entire system …
To use a telegraph; to send a message by telegraph.
To clearly communicate to another nonverbally (whether by gesture, a change in attitude, or any other sign), and especially unintentionally.

telegraph.ety: Borrowed from French télégraphe, equivalent to tele- (“far, distant”) + -graph (“writing”), suggested as a new name for Claude Chappe's overland semaphore network by André François Miot de Mélito in place of Chappe's original tachygraphe (“tachygraph, fast writer”).

ex.en: My parents telegraphed me to come back at once.
ex.ja: 両親からすぐに帰れと電報が来た。

ex.en: They telegraphed that everything was all right.
ex.ja: 彼らは万事異状なしということを電報で伝えた。

ex.en: The office telegraphed that they had not received my application.
ex.ja: 事務局は私の願書を受け取っていないと電報で知らせてきた。

note.ja: tele（遠く）+ graph（書く）。遠くへ書き送る仕組み →「電信・電報」。

en: Of, pertaining to, caused by, or characteristic of cowpox.
Of or pertaining to cowpox as a source of material for vaccination against smallpox; also, of or pertaining to such material used for vac…
A substance given to stimulate a body's production of antibodies and provide immunity against a disease without causing the disease itsel…
The process of vaccination; immunization, inoculation.

vaccine.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin vaccīnus (“of or derived from a cow”), from vacca (“cow (female cattle)”) + -īnus (suffix meaning ‘of or pertaining to’ forming adjectives). Sense 1 refers to the early use of the cowpox virus as a vaccination against smallpox: see New Latin variolae vaccīnae (“cowpox”, plural, literally “infectious diseases of cattle causing pustules”), coined by the British physician and scientist Edward Jenner (1749–1823).

ex.en: I haven't had the vaccine for Coronavirus.
ex.ja: コロナワクチンは打ってないです。

ex.en: I will not take the Corona vaccine.
ex.ja: コロナワクチンは受けないよ。

ex.en: I haven't had the COVID vaccine.
ex.ja: コロナワクチンは打ってないです。

note.ja: ラテン語 vacca（牛）から。牛痘（牛の天然痘）を使った種痘から名づけられた。

en: The univalent radical CH₂=CH−, derived from ethylene.
Any of various compounds and substances containing the vinyl radical, especially various tough, flexible, shiny plastics.
Containing the vinyl radical.
Made of polyvinyl chloride.

vinyl.ety:
Etymology tree

Proto-Italic *wīnom

English vinyl
From Latin vīnum (“wine”) + English -yl. Derived from Latin vīnum because ethyl alcohol is the ordinary alcohol present in wine.

ex.en: The weakness of vinyl is that it is easily affected by heat.
ex.ja: ビニールは熱に弱いのが難点だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 vinum（ワイン）+ -yl（化学の語尾）。エチルアルコールと関係する化学基の名前から。

en: In an accurate manner; exactly; precisely; without error or defect.

accurately.ety:
Etymology tree
English accurate
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English accurately
From accurate + -ly.

ex.en: He accurately described what happened there.
ex.ja: 彼はそこで起きたことを正確に描写した。

ex.en: Answer accurately in one go.
ex.ja: 一遍で正確に答えてください。

ex.en: I don't remember my father's face accurately.
ex.ja: 僕は父の顔を正確には覚えていない。

note.ja: accurate（正確な）+ -ly。ad（〜に）+ cura（注意・世話）。「注意を払った」→「正確な」。cure（治す）、care と関連。

en: Someone or something, especially, a television station, that is associated with a larger, related organization, such as a television netw…
To adopt; to receive into a family as one's offspring
to bring or receive into close connection; to ally.

affiliate.ety: From Medieval Latin affīliātus, the passive past participle of Late Latin adfīliō, affīliō (“to adopt as son”), from ad- + fīlius + -ō. Equivalent to Latin affīliō + -ate. Compare French affilié (noun).

ex.en: Our club is affiliated with an international organization.
ex.ja: 我々のクラブは国際的な組織に加入した。

ex.en: The college is affiliated with the university.
ex.ja: そのカレッジは大学に付属している。

ex.en: Why did you decide to affiliate yourself with Company A?
ex.ja: なぜ、Ａ社の傘下に入ることを選んだのか。

note.ja: ad（〜に）+ filius（息子）。「養子にする」→「傘下に入れる・提携させる」。filial（子としての）。

en: A place of safety or refuge.
The protection, physical and legal, afforded by such a place (as, for example, for political refugees).

asylum.ety:

Proto-Indo-European *n̥-

English asylum
Learned borrowing from Latin asȳlum, borrowed from Ancient Greek ἄσυλον (ásulon).

ex.en: Society is an insane asylum run by the inmates.
ex.ja: 社会は患者によって運営されている精神病院です。

ex.en: The embassy denied political asylum to foreign refugees.
ex.ja: 大使館は外国人難民の政治亡命を拒否しました。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 asylon（侵されない場所）から。a（否定）+ sylē（略奪）。「略奪されない所」→「避難所・亡命」。

en: A building, often found on a farm, used for storage or keeping animals such as cattle.
A unit of surface area equal to 10⁻²⁸ square metres.
To lay up in a barn.

barn.ety:
From Middle English barn, bern, bærn, from Old English bearn, bern, contracted forms of Old English berern, bereærn (“barn, granary”), compound of bere (“barley”) and ærn, ræn (“dwelling, barn”), from Proto-West Germanic *raʀn, from Proto-Germanic *razną (compare Old Norse rann), from pre-Germanic *h₁rh̥₁-s-nó-, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁erh₁- (“to rest”).
More at rest and barley.
For the use as a unit of surface area, see w:Barn (unit) § Etymology.

ex.en: The barn was small, but it was strong.
ex.ja: その納屋は小さかったが頑丈だった。

ex.en: Don't keep the car in the barn.
ex.ja: 納屋に自動車を置いてはいけません。

ex.en: On entering the barn, he found a missing bike.
ex.ja: 納屋に入るやいなや、彼はなくなった自転車を見つけた。

note.ja: 古英語 bere（大麦）+ ærn（家）。「大麦の家」→「納屋」。

en: Relating to the office of a bishop or an archbishop.
The principal church serving as the office (and some as place of residence) of an archdiocese's/a diocese's archbishop/bishop which is sy…
A large or important church building.

cathedral.ety: From Middle English cathedral, chathedral, cathiderall, from Old French [Term?], from Latin cathedrālis, from cathedra + -ālis, from Ancient Greek καθέδρα (kathédra, “chair of a teacher, throne”).

ex.en: The cathedral dates back to the Middle Ages.
ex.ja: その大聖堂の建立は中世にまでさかのぼる。

ex.en: This magnificent cathedral dates back to the Middle Ages.
ex.ja: この壮大な大聖堂の建立は中世にまでさかのぼる。

ex.en: The cathedral had a religious painting on its ceiling.
ex.ja: その大寺院の天井には宗教画が描かれていた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 kathedra（座席）から。kata（下に）+ hedra（座る所）。「司教の座がある教会」→「大聖堂」。chair（椅子）も同じ kathedra から。

en: A group of words that contains a subject and a verb; it may be part of a sentence or may constitute the whole sentence, depending on the …
A verb, its necessary grammatical arguments, and any adjuncts affecting them.
To amend (a bill of lading or similar document).

clause.ety: From Middle English clause, claus, borrowed from Old French clause, from Medieval Latin clausa (Latin diminutive clausula (“close, end; a clause, close of a period”)), from Latin clausus, past participle of claudere (“to shut, close”). See close, its doublet.

ex.en: The clause provides that all decisions shall be made by majority vote.
ex.ja: その条項は、議決はすべて過半数をもって成立すると規定している。

ex.en: Adverbial time clauses (here 'when') write about the future in the present tense.
ex.ja: 時の副詞節(ここではwhen)は、未来のことがらを現在時制で表します。

note.ja: ラテン語 claudere（閉じる）から。「区切られた（閉じた）一まとまり」→「節・条項」。close、include も同じ。

en: A bunch or group of several discrete items that are close to each other.
A group of galaxies, nebulae, or stars that appear to the naked eye to be near each other.
To collect (animals, people, objects, data points, etc) into clusters (noun sense 1).
To cover (with clusters); to scatter or strew in clusters (within); to distribute (objects) within such that they form clusters.

cluster.ety:
The noun is derived from Middle English cluster (“bunch, cluster, spray; compact body or mass, ball”) [and other forms], from Old English cluster, clyster (“cluster, bunch, branch”), from Proto-Germanic *klas-, *klus- (“to clump, lump together”) (possibly from Proto-Indo-European *gel- (“to ball up; to clench; to amass”)) + *-þrą (suffix forming nouns denoting an instrument or tool). The English word is probably a doublet of clot.
The verb is derived from the noun.
Cognates
* Dutch klister (“cluster”) (dialectal)
* Icelandic klasi (“cluster; bunch of grapes”)
* Low German Kluuster (“cluster”)

ex.en: They clustered around the fire.
ex.ja: 彼らは火の周りに集まった。

note.ja: 古英語 clyster（房）から。clot（固まり）と同系。「ひとかたまり」→「房・集団」。

en: Local coherence.
Correspondence or compatibility.

consistency.ety: By surface analysis, consistent + -cy, consistence + -y or consist + -ency.

ex.en: The main thing that dreams lack is consistency.
ex.ja: 夢に欠けている主な事は首尾一貫性である。

ex.en: Corn starch gives the white sauce its consistency.
ex.ja: コーンスターチで、ホワイトソースにとろみがつきます。

note.ja: consist（成り立つ・一致する）+ -ency。con（共に）+ sistere（立つ）。「一緒に立っていること」→「一貫性」。insist、resist も同じ。

en: A surface created by projecting a closed two-dimensional curve along an axis intersecting the plane of the curve.
A solid figure bounded by a cylinder and two parallel planes intersecting the cylinder.
To calender; to press (paper, etc.) between rollers to make it glossy.

cylinder.ety: From Middle French chilindre, cylindre, from Latin cylindrus, from Ancient Greek κύλινδρος (kúlindros), from κυλίνδω (kulíndō) "I roll or wallow" (intransitive). Doublet of calander and calender.

ex.en: The gas was compressed into a gas cylinder.
ex.ja: その気体は圧縮されてボンベに詰め込まれた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 kylindros（転がるもの）から。kylindein（転がす）。「転がる筒」→「円柱・シリンダー」。

en: A person who dances, usually as a hobby, an occupation, or a profession.
A stripper.

dancer.ety: From Middle English dauncer, dawncere, dancere, equivalent to dance + -er.

ex.en: That is, she is a poor dancer.
ex.ja: つまり彼女は下手な踊り子だ。

ex.en: Unfortunately, I'm not much of a dancer.
ex.ja: 残念だけど、ダンスはあまり得意じゃないんだ。

ex.en: I think she is a good dancer.
ex.ja: 私は彼女は踊りが上手だと思います。

note.ja: dance + -er。dance は古フランス語 dancier から。

en: Unable (or partially able) to hear.
Unwilling to listen or be persuaded; determinedly inattentive.

deaf.ety:
From Middle English def, deef, from Old English dēaf, from Proto-West Germanic *daub (“deaf”), from Proto-Germanic *daubaz (“deaf or stunned”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰewbʰ- (“to whisk, smoke, darken, obscure”). Cognate with Ancient Greek τυφλός (tuphlós, “blind”). See also dumb. Doublet of daff, dof, and dowf.
Cognate with Dutch doof, German taub, Danish and Norwegian Bokmål døv, Norwegian Nynorsk dauv, Swedish döv, Faroese deyvur, Icelandic daufur.

ex.en: She goes to a school for the deaf.
ex.ja: 彼女は耳の不自由な人々のための学校に通っている。

ex.en: He turned a deaf ear to my advice.
ex.ja: 彼は忠告に耳を貸さなかった。

ex.en: I wonder whether Tom is really going deaf.
ex.ja: トムは本当に耳が聞こえなくなってきてるのかな。

note.ja: 古英語 dēaf から。ドイツ語 taub と同じ。「ぼんやりした・感覚が鈍い」が原義とされる。

en: An assertion of untruth.
The negation in logic.

denial.ety:

From deny + -al.

ex.en: The police didn't believe his denial.
ex.ja: 警察は彼が否定したのを真に受けなかった。

note.ja: deny（否定する）+ -al。de（完全に）+ negare（いいえと言う）。negative と同じ。

en: Any of the genus Rumex of coarse weedy plants with small green flowers related to buckwheat, especially bitter dock (Rumex obtusifolius),…
A burdock plant, or the leaves of that plant.
To clip or cut off a section of an animal's tail; to practise a caudectomy.
To reduce (wages); to deduct from (someone).

dock.ety: From Middle English dokke, from Old English docce, from Proto-West Germanic *dokkā, from Proto-Germanic *dukkǭ (compare Old Danish dokke (“water-dock”), West Flemish dokke, dokkebladeren (“coltsfoot, butterbur”)), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰew- (“dark”) (compare Latvian duga (“scum, slime on water”)).

ex.en: There was no one on the dock.
ex.ja: 埠頭には誰もいなかった。

ex.en: The huge tanker has just left the dock.
ex.ja: 巨大なタンカーがついに今し方出港した。

ex.en: A huge tanker just pulled out from the dock.
ex.ja: 巨大なタンカーがついに今し方出港した。

note.ja: 中世オランダ語 docke（水路・船着き場）から。「船を入れる場所」→「ドック・波止場」。宇宙船の docking も同じ。

en: A person who sets up a business; generally, a person who owns and manages a business and assumes its financial risks.

entrepreneur.ety: Borrowed from French entrepreneur (“one who undertakes or manages”), from Middle French entrepreneur, from entreprendre (“to undertake”) + -eur.

ex.en: Scott is an entrepreneur with much spirit of enterprise.
ex.ja: スコットさんは企業家精神に富む経営者なんです。

ex.en: Everyone is an entrepreneur.
ex.ja: だれもが「企業家」なのである。

ex.en: His claim is really the same as the one Benson proposed in Entrepreneurs.
ex.ja: 彼の主張はベンソンが『Ｅｎｔｒｅｐｒｅｎｅｕｒｓ』で主張していることと事実上同じである。

note.ja: フランス語 entreprendre（企てる）から。entre（間に）+ prendre（取る）。「手に取って引き受ける人」→「起業家」。enterprise と同じ。

en: Obviously true by simple observation.

evident.ety: From Middle English evident, from Old French evident, from Latin ēvidēns (“visible, apparent, clear, plain”) (compare Late Latin ēvideor (“to appear plainly”)), from ē (“out”) + videō (“see”), present participle vidēns, deponent videor (“to appear, seem”). Displaced native Old English sweotol.

ex.en: It is evident that the man is wrong.
ex.ja: その男が間違っているのは明らかだ。

ex.en: It's evident to everybody that he's in love.
ex.ja: 彼が恋をしているのは明らかだ。

ex.en: It is evident that the Earth is round.
ex.ja: 地球が丸いということは今では明らかである。

note.ja: e（外へ・はっきり）+ vid（見る）+ ent。はっきり見える →「明白な」。evidence（証拠）。

en: A military journey; an enterprise against some enemy or into enemy territory.
An important or long journey, for example a march or a voyage.
To take part in a trip or expedition; to travel.

expedition.ety: From Middle French expédition, and its source, Latin expeditio.

ex.en: His death brought the expedition to an end.
ex.ja: 彼の死でその探索は中止された。

ex.en: I watched the expedition as it set off.
ex.ja: 私は一行が出発するのを見守った。

ex.en: He was the leader of the great expedition.
ex.ja: 彼はその大遠征のリーダーだった。

note.ja: ラテン語 expedire（足かせを外す）から。ex（外へ）+ pes（足）。「足を自由にして進む」→「遠征・探検」。pedal、pedestrian も同じ pes。

en: To make easy or easier.
To help bring about.

facilitate.ety: Anglicisation of French faciliter (“facilitate”) through -ate (verb-forming suffix), ultimately from Latin facilis.

ex.en: We have established the institute with a view to facilitating the research.
ex.ja: われわれは研究を促進するために、この協会を設立した。

note.ja: ラテン語 facilis（容易な）から。fac（する）。容易にする →「促進する・手助けする」。

en: A relatively rare or difficult accomplishment.
To feature.

feat.ety: From Middle English [Term?], from Anglo-Norman fet (“action, deed”), from Old French fait, from Latin factum, from facere (“to do, to make”). Doublet of fact.

ex.en: The player performed a wonderful feat.
ex.ja: その選手は妙技を演じた。

ex.en: Her skating performance was a regular feat.

Goods or items in transport; cargo, luggage.
To load (a vehicle or vessel) with freight (cargo); also, to hire or rent out (a vehicle or vessel) to carry cargo or passengers.
To transport (goods).

en: The act, quality, or condition of being honest.
Any of various crucifers in the genus Lunaria, several of which are grown as ornamentals, particularly annual honesty (Lunaria annua).

honesty.ety: From Middle English honeste (“honour, integrity”), from Old French honesté (compare modern French honnêteté). By surface analysis, honest + -y. Displaced native Old English sōþfæstnes and non-native Middle English prodonomee, from Old French prodomie. The plant is named so after the visibility of the seeds through the translucent pods.

Improper; adult; sexual.

A minor.

infant.ety: Inherited from Middle English infaunt, borrowed from Latin īnfantem, accusative masculine singular of īnfāns, nominal use of the adjective meaning 'not able to speak', from īn- (“not”) + fāns, present participle of for (“to speak”). The verb is from Anglo-Norman enfanter, from the same Latin source. Doublet of infante.

ex.en: We need more medical care for infants.
ex.ja: 乳幼児に対する医療がもっと必要である。

ex.ja: その若い女は腕に幼児を抱いていた。

ex.en: Infants are subject to diseases.
ex.ja: 幼児は病気にかかりやすい。

note.ja: ラテン語 infans（話せない）から。in（否定）+ fari（話す）。「まだ話せない子」→「乳児」。infantry（歩兵：若い兵）も同じ。fable（話）、fate（語られたこと → 運命）も同じ fari。

en: To begin; to start.
To instruct in the rudiments or principles; to introduce.
A new member of an organization.
One who has been through a ceremony of initiation.

initiate.ety: Borrowed from Latin initiātus, perfect passive participle of initiō (“to begin, originate”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from initium (“a beginning”) + -ō (verb-forming suffix), from initus (“an entrance, coming in, approach”) + -ium, from ineō + -tus, from in- + eō (“to go”). Cognate with French initier.

note.ja: in（中へ）+ it（行く）+ iate。中へ入らせる →「始める・入会させる」。

en: The act of injecting, or something that is injected.
A specimen prepared by injection.

injection.ety: Borrowed from Middle French injection, from Latin iniectio. The mathematical sense is from French injection, introduced by Nicolas Bourbaki in their treatise Éléments de mathématique. Equivalent to inject + -ion.

ex.en: He had an injection prior to the operation.
ex.ja: 手術の前に彼は注射をされた。

ex.ja: 注射をしときますね。

ex.ja: 看護婦は私に注射した。

Serving as an instrument, medium, means, or agency.

ex.ja: 彼は日本を理解させるのに非常に力があった。

Something that causes offence (for example, by being of an unacceptable quality).

The illegal obstruction of an opponent in some ball games.

note.ja: interfere（干渉する）+ -ence。inter（間）+ ferire（打つ）。「間に入って打つ」→「干渉・妨害」。

en: Clean, tidy; free from dirt or impurities.
Free from contaminants or impurities, unadulterated.
Used to signify a job well done.
Used to signify approval.
An artificial intelligence researcher who believes that solutions should be elegant, clear and provably correct. Compare scruffy.

Doublet of net and nitid. Cognate with German nett (“nice, kind”). Compare also nait.

ex.ja: 自分の部屋は出来るだけきちんとしておきたい。

ex.ja: 彼の部屋は小奇麗とは到底言えない。

en: To confer with others in order to come to terms or reach an agreement.
To arrange or settle something by mutual agreement.

negotiate.ety: c. 1598; borrowed from Latin negōtiātus, perfect active participle of negōtior (“to do business, trade”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from negotium (“business”) + -or, from nec (“not”) + otium (“leisure, ease, inactivity”).

ex.ja: 労働組合は経営陣と交渉している。

ex.ja: 我々は就労時間について社長と交渉した。

ex.en: They wanted to negotiate the contract on equal terms.

To place out of line.
Away from or off from the set of a movie, film, video, or play.
Away from or off from the set of a movie, film, video, or play.

ex.en: A bigger harvest should help offset the expected drop in crop prices.
ex.ja: 収穫高の増加は、来る穀物価格の下落による影響を緩和するのに役立つであろう。

note.ja: off（離れて）+ set（置く）。「反対側に置いて釣り合わせる」→「相殺する・埋め合わせる」。

A sudden increase.

ex.ja: その突発について不必要に心配する必要はない。

en: A friend, buddy, mate, cobber; someone to hang around with.
An informal term of address, often used ironically in a hostile way.

perfection.ety: From Middle English perfeccioun, from Old French perfection, from Latin perfectiō. By surface analysis, perfect + -ion. Displaced native Old English fulfremednes.

ex.ja: 彼は絵画の技法を完成させた。

ex.en: The Venus de Milo is the perfection of beauty.
ex.ja: ミロのヴィーナスは美の極致だ。

ex.en: Mayuko always aims for perfection.
ex.ja: マユコはいつも完璧を目指している。

A person enlisted for service in the army; a newly enlisted soldier.

en: The process of rehabilitating somebody or something.

rehabilitation.ety: From Middle French réhabilitation, from Medieval Latin rehabilitatio.

ex.en: He came to take a walk every morning after rehabilitation.
ex.ja: 彼はリハビリの後、毎朝散歩するようになりました。

ex.ja: コストダウンもできない生ぬるいリストラがJAL再建を危うくする。

ex.ja: ビオラは耐寒性植物だよ。

ex.en: This car is resistant to rust.
ex.ja: この車は錆に強い。

note.ja: resist（抵抗する）+ -ant。re（逆らって）+ sistere（立つ）。「逆らって立つ」→「抵抗力のある」。

en: Any rotating cylindrical device that is part of a machine, especially one used to apply or reduce pressure.
A cylindrical (or approximately cylindrical) item used under a heavy object to facilitate moving it; usually several are needed.
To roller skate.

ex.ja: 私はそのローラースケートをただで手に入れた。

ex.ja: この公園でローラースケートをしてもいいですか。

ex.ja: 彼女にローラースケートの仕方を教えてやりなさい。

note.ja: roll（転がる）+ -er。roll はラテン語 rota（車輪）の縮小 rotula から。rotate（回転する）と同じ。

en: Thin, generally in a negative sense (as opposed to slim, which is thin in a positive sense).
Of food or a beverage, having reduced fat or calories.
The details or facts; especially, those obtained by gossip or rumor.
A state of nakedness; nudity.

ex.ja: その男はやせているが、彼の妻は太っている。

ex.ja: 茶色くて、小さくて、やせっぽちの犬です。

Doublet of cirque. Cognate with Old English hring (whence English ring) and Old English hringsetl (“circus”, literally “ring-seat”).

ex.en: Tom didn't want to go to the circus with Mary.
ex.ja: トムはメアリーとは一緒にサーカスに行きたくなかった。

ex.en: Everyone turned out for the circus.
ex.ja: サーカスを見にみんなくりだした。

ex.en: I don't want to go to the circus with Tom.
ex.ja: トムとは一緒にサーカスに行きたくない。

note.ja: ラテン語 circus（円・円形競技場）から。circle（円）と同じ。「円形の見世物場」→「サーカス」。

en: An addictive drug derived from coca (Erythroxylum) or prepared synthetically, used sometimes medicinally as a local anesthetic and, often…
The powder form of this drug, specifically.
Synonym of cocainize.

cocaine.ety:

ex.ja: 彼はコカインに溺れている。

en: To make by gathering pieces from various sources.
To achieve (a break) by making a sequence of shots.
An act of compiling code.

compile.ety: From Middle English compilen, from Old French compiler, from Latin compīlō (“to plunder”).

ex.en: I spent three months compiling this data.
ex.ja: このデータを集めるのに三ヶ月を費やした。

ex.en: The data hasn't been compiled yet.
ex.ja: データはまだまとめていません。

ex.en: Compile an essay on that topic within a fixed number of letters.
ex.ja: それについて、決められた字数以内に作文を纏める。

note.ja: ラテン語 compilare（略奪する・かき集める）から。「いろいろ集めてまとめる」→「編集する」、プログラムをまとめて機械語に →「コンパイルする」。

en: The act or process of complicating.
The state of being complicated; intricate or confused relation of parts; complexity.

complication.ety: Borrowed from Middle French complication, from Latin complicatio, complicationem. Morphologically complicate + -ion.

note.ja: com（共に）+ plic（折る）+ ation。折り重なってもつれること →「面倒な事態・合併症」。

en: A long, thin, flexible length of twisted yarns (strands) of fibre (a rope, for example).
Any quantity of such material when viewed as a mass or commodity.
To furnish with cords.
To tie or fasten with cords.

cord.ety: From Middle English corde, from Old French corde, from Latin chorda, from Ancient Greek χορδή (khordḗ, “string of gut, the string of a lyre”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰerH- (“bowels, intestines”). Displaced native Old English sīma (“cord, rope”), sāl (“rope, cord, rein”), and sāda (“cord, halter, snare”). Doublet of chord and cuerda. More at yarn and hernia.

ex.en: He connected the cord to the machine.
ex.ja: 彼は機械にコードをつないだ。

ex.en: They made a whip out of cords.
ex.ja: 細縄で鞭を作った。

ex.en: Do fish have vocal cords?
ex.ja: 魚に声帯はありますか？

note.ja: ギリシャ語 khordē（腸で作った弦）から。→「ひも・コード・（楽器の）弦」。※ cor（心）とは別語源。chord（和音）も同じ。

en: A valley, often in an otherwise hilly area.
The sunken or grooved portion of the surface of a vinyl record.

dale.ety: From Middle English dale, from Old English dæl, from Proto-West Germanic *dal, from Proto-Germanic *dalą.

note.ja: 古英語 dæl（谷）から。ドイツ語 Tal と同じ。

en: Serving, or suitable, for defense; defensive, defending.
In civil proceedings, the party responding to the complaint; one who is sued and called upon to make satisfaction for a wrong complained …
In criminal proceedings, the accused.

defendant.ety: From Middle English defendaunt (“defending; defending in a suit”), borrowed from Old French defendant, present participle of defendre, from Latin dēfendere.

ex.en: The defendant will appeal to a higher court.
ex.ja: 被告は上級裁判所に控訴するだろう。

ex.en: The decision was in favor of the defendant.
ex.ja: 判決は被告に有利だった。

ex.en: The defendant was granted an appeal.
ex.ja: 被告は上告を認められた。

note.ja: defend（守る）+ -ant。「（訴えに対して）自分を守る人」→「被告」。de（離して）+ fendere（打つ）。offend（攻撃する）、fence（defence の略）も同じ。

en: Having relatively high density.
Compact; crowded together.
A thicket.

dense.ety: From Middle French dense, from Latin dēnsus, from Proto-Indo-European *dens- (“thick, dense”) (whence also Ancient Greek δασύς (dasús)).

ex.en: There is a dense population of young people around here.
ex.ja: このあたりは若者が密集することが多い。

ex.en: The man was hiding in a dense forest.
ex.ja: 男はこんもりした森に隠れていた。

ex.en: Mr Smith lost his way in the dense fog.
ex.ja: スミスさんは濃霧の中で道に迷った。

note.ja: ラテン語 densus（濃い・密な）から。density（密度）、condense（凝縮する）も同じ。

en: In a desperate manner; without regard to danger or safety; recklessly.
Extremely.

desperately.ety:
Etymology tree
English desperate
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English desperately
From desperate + -ly.

ex.en: He's desperately trying to make up for the delay.
ex.ja: 彼は遅れを取り戻そうと焦っている。

ex.en: She wanted desperately to get her vengeance.
ex.ja: 彼女はなんとかして復讐しようと焦っていた。

note.ja: desperate（必死の）+ -ly。de（離れて）+ sperare（希望する）。「希望を失った」→「やけになった → 必死の」。

en: A belief or tenet, especially about philosophical or theological matters.
The body of teachings of an ideology, most often a religion, or of an ideological or religious leader, organization, group, or text.

doctrine.ety: From Middle English, from Old French, from Latin doctrina (“teaching, instruction, learning, knowledge”), from doctor (“a teacher”), from docere (“to teach”); see doctor.

ex.en: That doctrine will no doubt lead to serious consequences.
ex.ja: その主義はおそらく重大な結果を招くだろう。

ex.en: That doctrine will no doubt lead to dismal consequences.
ex.ja: その主義はきっと良くない結果を招くだろう。

ex.en: Tom has a doctrine of "not rocking the boat".
ex.ja: トムは事なかれ主義だからね。

note.ja: ラテン語 docere（教える）から。「教えられた内容」→「教義・主義」。doctor（教える人）、document も同じ。

ex.ja: 去年の新人です。

ex.en: Tom is a college freshman.
ex.ja: トムは1回生です。

ex.en: Tom is a freshman.
ex.ja: トムは1回生です。

note.ja: fresh（新しい）+ man。「新しく入った者」→「1年生・新入生」。

en: Feeling great anger; raging; violent.
Rushing with impetuosity; moving with violence.

furious.ety: From Middle English furious, from Old French furieus, from Latin furiōsus. Displaced native Old English hātheort (literally “hot-hearted”).

ex.en: I said nothing, which made him more furious.
ex.ja: 私は何も言わなかった、そしてそのことで彼は一層激怒した。

ex.en: Our latest results are the fruit of his furious efforts.
ex.ja: 今回の成果はひとえに彼の獅子奮迅の働きの賜物でしょう。

ex.en: He is furious at what they have done to him.
ex.ja: 彼は彼らの仕打ちに激怒している。

note.ja: fury（激怒）+ -ous。ラテン語 furia（怒り狂うこと）から。ローマ神話の復讐の女神 Furiae。

en: The totality of player experiences during a game, such as the gaming environment and the competitive interaction with other players; ofte…

ex.en: Watching gameplay videos online made me want to play it for myself.
ex.ja: 実況プレイをネットで見て、自分もやろうと思ったんだ。

note.ja: game + play。「ゲームの遊び方・遊び心地」。

en: Originally (music), a performing engagement by a musician or musical group; (by extension, film, television, theater) a job or role for a…
Any job, especially one that is freelance or temporary, or done on an on-demand basis.
To play (a musical instrument) at a gig.
To impose a demerit (on someone) for an infraction of a military deportment or dress code.

gig.ety: The etymology of the noun is unknown, but compare Old French gigue (“a fiddle”). The verb is derived from the noun.

note.ja: ジャズ・ミュージシャンの俗語から。「1回の演奏の仕事」→「ライブ・仕事」。

en: Conditions suitable for an organism or population of organisms to live.
A range; a place where a species naturally occurs.

habitat.ety: From Latin habitat (“it dwells, lives”), the 3rd person singular present active indicative form of habitō (“to live or dwell”). In Linnaeus and similar authors, the geographical ranges of species were customarily denoted in Latin by a sentence beginning with "Habitat", e.g. "Habitat in Europa" ("It lives in Europe"), and it thus became the convention to refer to the geographical range as the "habitat". Compare the English derivations of exit, floruit, ignoramus, and tenet from Latin finite verbs reanalyzed as English nouns.

ex.en: Their habitat is threatened by deforestation.
ex.ja: 彼らの生息地は、森林破壊に脅かされています。

note.ja: ラテン語で「（それが）住む」。habitare（住む）から。「生き物が住む場所」→「生息地」。habit、inhabit も同じ habere（持つ）系。

en: A game of chance played with dice, usually for monetary stakes, popular mainly from 14th c. to 19th c.
Chance; accident, unpredictability.
To expose to chance; to take a risk.
To risk (something); to venture, incur, or bring on.

hazard.ety: From Middle English hasard, from Old French hasart (“a game of dice”) (noun), hasarder (verb), from Arabic اَلزَّهْر (az-zahr, “the dice”). Compare Spanish azar, Portuguese azar.

ex.en: This is a hazard to your health.
ex.ja: これはあなたの健康にとって危険なものだ。

note.ja: アラビア語 az-zahr（さいころ）から古フランス語を経て。「さいころ賭け」→「運任せ」→「危険」。

An atom of this element.

ex.ja: 水素はそれ自体としては自然界に存在しない。

ex.en: Water is made of hydrogen and oxygen.
ex.ja: 水は水素と酸素で出来ている。

ex.en: Water consists of hydrogen and oxygen.
ex.ja: 水は水素と酸素とから成り立っている。

note.ja: hydr（水）+ o + gen（生む）。燃やすと水を生むもの →「水素」。

en: To have as a necessary consequence; to lead to (something) as a consequence.
To suggest by logical inference.

imply.ety: From Middle English implien, emplien, borrowed from Old French emplier, from Latin implicare (“to infold, involve”), from in (“in”) + plicare (“to fold”). Doublet of employ and implicate.

ex.en: None of them could understand what she was implying.
ex.ja: 彼らのうち誰一人、彼女がほのめかしたことを理解できなかった。

ex.en: She implied that she would like to come with us.
ex.ja: 彼女は我々と行きたいのだとほのめかした。

ex.en: What do his words imply?
ex.ja: 彼の言葉は何を暗示しているのか。

note.ja: im（中に）+ ply（折る）。中に折り込む →「ほのめかす・暗に意味する」。implication（含意）。

en: The place where water, air or other fluid is taken into a pipe or conduit; opposed to outlet.
The beginning of a contraction or narrowing in a tube or cylinder.
To take in or draw in; to bring in from outside.

intake.ety: From English dialectal (Northern England/Scotland), deverbal of take in, equivalent to in- + take. More at in-, take.

ex.en: You won't lose weight unless you cut back on your food intake.
ex.ja: ごはんの量を減らさなければ、痩せません。

ex.en: After his heart attack, Jim had to cut down on his sugar intake.
ex.ja: 心臓発作の後、ジムは砂糖の摂取量をへらさなければならなかった。

ex.en: Please limit your fluid intake.
ex.ja: 水分を控えてください。

note.ja: in（中に）+ take（取る）。「中に取り込むこと」→「摂取（量）・取り入れ口」。

en: Not relevant, as
Not at all related: totally unrelated, wholly unconnected, completely inapplicable.

Proto-Italic *n̥-

ex.en: What he said is irrelevant to the matter.
ex.ja: 彼の言ったことはその問題に関係ない。

ex.ja: ちょっと全然関係ないこと聞いてもいい？

ex.en: Your suggestion seems irrelevant to our discussion here.
ex.ja: あなたの提案はここの議論とは無関係のように思われます。

note.ja: ir（否定）+ relevant（関連のある）。relevant はラテン語 relevare（持ち上げる・助けになる）から。「役に立つ → 関係がある」の否定。relieve と同じ。

en: One of the bones, usually bearing teeth, which form the framework of the mouth.
The part of the face below the mouth.
To assail or abuse by scolding.
To scold; to clamor.

jaw.ety:
From Middle English jawe/jowe (“jaw; sides of the lower face”, 14th century), the further origin of which is disputed. Either:
* From Anglo-Norman jowe, from Old French joe (“cheek; jaw”), from Vulgar Latin *ga(v)ota (“cheek”), of uncertain further origin.
** It has been objected that the rhyming of jowe (“jaw”) with clowe (“claw”) in Middle English demonstrates that it did not have the vowel /uː/. This would be a concern if /uː/ were the vowel to expect from a borrowing of the Old French word, which it is not. Compare English paw < Middle English pawe/powe < Anglo-Norman powe < Old French poe

ex.en: When I heard about it, my jaw dropped.
ex.ja: 聞いた時、開いた口が塞がらなかったよ。

ex.en: He got a broken jaw and lost some teeth.
ex.ja: 彼は顎の骨を折って、歯も何本か折れた。

ex.en: As his eyes ran over the paper, his jaw fell.
ex.ja: 一通り読み終えたところで、あんぐり口を開けた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 joue（頬）からとされる。「あご」。

en: A young cat; a kitten.
An adult cat; also (often childish), sometimes in the form Kitty: a pet name for a cat of any age.

kitty.ety:
From kitt(en) + -y (diminutive suffix). Compare Dutch katje (“kitty”).
Etymology 1 sense 2 (“vulva and/or vagina”) is probably modelled after the use of pussy to refer to the body part, from the appearance of an unshaven vulva.

ex.en: I have a kitty and a dog.
ex.ja: 子猫と犬を飼ってます。

ex.en: I want two kitties.
ex.ja: ２匹、ニャンコが欲しい。

ex.en: That's not for kitties!
ex.ja: それは子猫のためじゃないよ。

note.ja: kit（kitten の短縮）+ -y。子猫を呼ぶ愛称。kitten は cat の縮小形。

An open space between woods.
To furnish with a lawn.

ex.ja: 母は私に芝を刈るように言った。

To tease in order to provoke; to poke fun at.

ex.ja: とりわけ人目をひいたのは、彼女の卵型の顔立ちだった。

ex.ja: アブミ骨は内耳の前庭窓に接している。

en: A feeling of sympathy at the misfortune or suffering of someone or something.
Feeling of contempt one has for someone who is hopelessly inferior.
To feel pity for (someone or something).
To feel contempt for someone who is hopelessly inferior.

ex.ja: 君が日本を離れるのは残念だ。

ex.en: It is a pity that he can't come.
ex.ja: 彼が来れないのは残念だ。

ex.en: I do think that it is a pity.
ex.ja: 本当に残念だと思う。

note.ja: ラテン語 pietas（敬虔・義務感）から。piety（敬虔）と同じ語源で、後に意味が分かれた。

en: An inland body of standing water, either natural or man-made, that is smaller than a lake.
An inland body of standing water of any size that is fed by springs rather than by a river.
To block the flow of water so that it can escape only through evaporation or seepage; to dam.
To make into a pond; to collect, as water, in a pond by damming.

pond.ety: From Middle English pond, ponde (“pond, pool”), probably from Old English *pond, *pand (attested in placenames), a variant of *pund (“enclosure”). Doublet of pound.

ex.en: Children should be kept away from the pond.
ex.ja: 子供は池に近づかないように。

ex.en: There is much water in the pond today.
ex.ja: 今日は池にたくさんの水があります。

ex.en: There used to be a pond around here.
ex.ja: 以前このあたりに池があった。

note.ja: pound（家畜の囲い）と同じ語。「水をせき止めて囲った所」→「池」。

en: A person who carries luggage and related objects; (historically) one who carried luggage or did manual labour in the transloading of cargo.
An ant having the specialized role of carrying.
To serve as a porter; to carry.

porter.ety: From Middle English porter, portere, portier, borrowed from Anglo-Norman portour and Old French porteor, from Late Latin portātor, from past participle of Latin portāre (“to carry”). By surface analysis, port (“to carry”) + -er.

ex.en: Porters often have to walk across the tracks.
ex.ja: ポーターはしばしば線路を歩いて渡らなければならない。

ex.en: She had her heavy suitcase carried by the porter.
ex.ja: 彼女は重いスーツケースをポーターに運んでもらった。

ex.en: I had the porter carry my suitcase.
ex.ja: 私は赤帽にスーツケースを運んでもらった。

note.ja: port（運ぶ）+ er（人）。荷物を運ぶ人 →「荷物運搬人・ポーター」。

en: That which is or may be seized by animals to be devoured.
A person or thing given up as a victim.
To act as a predator.

prey.ety: From Middle English preye, prei, preyȝe, borrowed from Anglo-Norman and Old French preie, one of the variants of proie, from Latin praeda. Compare predator. Doublet of prede.

ex.en: The number of prey they killed was the same.
ex.ja: 彼らが殺したえじきの数はおなじだった。

ex.en: Some large birds prey upon small birds and animals.
ex.ja: 大きな鳥は小鳥や小動物を捕って食べるものもいる。

ex.en: Death is seeking for his prey.
ex.ja: 死神は餌食を求めている。

note.ja: ラテン語 praeda（獲物・戦利品）から。predator（捕食者）、depredation（略奪）も同じ。pray（祈る）とは別語。

en: Someone who speaks by divine inspiration.
Someone who predicts the future; a soothsayer.

prophet.ety: From Middle English prophete, from Anglo-Norman prophete, from Latin prophēta, from Ancient Greek προφήτης (prophḗtēs, “one who speaks for a god”), from πρό (pró, “before”) + φημί (phēmí, “to tell”). Displaced native Old English wītga.

ex.en: Are you the prophet?
ex.ja: あなたは預言者ですか。

ex.en: Once in a while, the prophet indulges in fantasy.
ex.ja: たまに、その預言者は空想にふける。

ex.en: Prophets have been forecasting the end of the world for centuries.
ex.ja: 預言者は何世紀もの間、この世の終わりを予言し続けてきた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 prophētēs から。pro（前に・代わりに）+ phanai（話す）。「神に代わって前もって語る人」→「預言者」。prophecy（予言）。

en: A direct popular vote on a proposed law or constitutional amendment.
An action, choice, etc., which is perceived as passing judgment on another matter.

referendum.ety: From Latin referendum (“that which ought to be announced”), from refero (“to announce”).

ex.en: The government put the question to the people in a referendum.
ex.ja: 政府が住民に問う一般投票を実施しました。

ex.en: Kilby applied Emmet's theory to his investigation of the referendum held in Greece in 1948.
ex.ja: キルビーは１９４８年のギリシャ国民投票にエメット理論を適用した。

note.ja: ラテン語 referre（持ち帰る・付託する）の動名詞。「国民に持ち帰って判断を委ねること」→「国民投票」。refer と同じ。

en: To dictate policy.
To control or direct according to rule, principle, or law.

regulate.ety: Borrowed from Latin regulatus, perfect passive participle of regulō (“to direct, rule, regulate”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from regula (“rule”), from regō (“to keep straight, direct, govern, rule”). Compare regle, rail. Displaced native Old English metegian.

ex.en: Traffic lights are used to regulate traffic.
ex.ja: 交通信号は交通の流れを規制するために使われている。

ex.en: Hong Kong is the least regulated economy in Asia.
ex.ja: 香港はアジアでは最も規制が少ない経済である。

ex.en: Rice prices are regulated by the government.
ex.ja: 米価は政府によって統制されている。

note.ja: ラテン語 regula（定規・規則）から。reg（まっすぐ）。定規に合わせる →「規制する・調整する」。regular（規則的な）、rule（規則）も同じ。

en: A clear, deep, red variety of corundum, valued as a precious stone.
A deep red colour.
Of a deep, red color; ruby-red.
To make red; to redden.

ruby.ety:
From Middle English ruby, rube, from Old French rubi, from Medieval Latin rubīnus. Doublet of rubi and rubine.
Etymology 1 sense 7 (“pronunciation guide”) is from the British 5½-point type size (etymology 1 sense 6), used for annotations in printed documents.

note.ja: ラテン語 rubeus（赤い）から。ruber（赤）。rubella（風疹：赤い発疹）も同じ。日本語の「ルビ（振り仮名）」は、昔の印刷で振り仮名に使う活字の大きさの名前（ruby）から。

en: Acting with or showing good sense; able to make good judgements based on reason or wisdom, or reflecting such ability.
Characterized more by usefulness, practicality, or comfort than by attractiveness, formality, or fashionableness, especially of clothing.

sensible.ety: From Latin sēnsibilis (“perceptible by the senses, having feeling, sensible”), from sentiō (“to feel, perceive”).

ex.en: What he says sounds very sensible to me.
ex.ja: 彼が言っていることは非常にもっともなことだ、と私には思われる。

ex.en: It is sensible of you to follow her advice.
ex.ja: 彼女の忠告に従うとは賢明ですね。

ex.en: A sensible person wouldn't speak to you like that.
ex.ja: 良識のある人ならそんな風に君に話しかけないだろう。

note.ja: sens（感じる）+ ible。分別をもって感じ取れる →「分別のある・賢明な」。※ sensitive（敏感な）と区別。

en: A narrative that is written after another narrative set in the same universe, especially a narrative that is chronologically set after it…
Synonym of postquel; a narrative work that follows-on and is set after an prior existing work.

sequel.ety: From Middle English sequele, sequelle, sequile, from Middle French sequele, sequelle and its etymon, Latin sequēla, from sequī (“to follow”). Doublet of sequela.

ex.en: By the way, I plan to do that for this story's sequel.
ex.ja: ちなみに、それはこの話の後日談にする予定です。

ex.en: Each sequel of this game contains fewer and fewer characters.
ex.ja: このゲーム、続編が出るたびにキャラが減ってるな。

note.ja: ラテン語 sequi（続く）から。sequ + el。後に続くもの →「続編・結果」。

en: To regard with wonder and delight.
To look upon with an elevated feeling of pleasure, as something which calls out approbation, esteem, love or reverence.

admire.ety: From Middle English admyren, borrowed from Middle French admirer, from Latin admīror, from ad + mīror (“wonder at”).

ex.en: My ability to improve has been admired everywhere.
ex.ja: 俺の改善力は各所で評価されたものだ。

ex.en: Yes. Everyone admires the pictures painted by him.
ex.ja: うん。みんなが彼の描く絵をほめているね。

ex.en: She stopped before the mirror to admire herself.
ex.ja: 彼女は鏡の前に立ち止まって、惚れ惚れと自分を眺めた。

note.ja: ad（〜に）+ mirari（驚く・不思議がる）。「驚嘆して見つめる」→「感心する・称賛する」。miracle（奇跡）、mirror（鏡）も同じ。

A yellow-orange colour.

ex.en: "When they say your pee is amber-colored, that means you're dehydrated."
ex.ja: 「小便が琥珀色だと言われたら、脱水症状だ」

note.ja: アラビア語 ʿanbar（龍涎香）から。のちに似た色の化石樹脂を指すようになった。

en: A person, especially a man, who is socially regarded as able to marry but has not yet.
A bachelor apartment.

bachelor.ety: From Middle English bacheler, from Anglo-Norman and Old French bacheler (modern French bachelier), from Medieval Latin baccalārius, baccalāris (compare Tuscan baccalare (“squire”)).

ex.en: Tom remained a bachelor until his death.

A careful attention to the probable effects of an act, in order that failure or harm may be avoided.
To warn; to alert, advise that caution is warranted.
To read someone their formal legal rights as part of a lawful arrest.

caution.ety: Recorded since 1297 as Middle English caucioun (“bail, guarantee, pledge”), from Old French caution (“security, surety”), itself from Latin cautiō, from cautus, past participle of caveō, cavēre (“be on one's guard”).

ex.en: Caution: risk of electric shock. Do not open.
ex.ja: あけるな危険。感電の可能性あり。

ex.en: I repeat it by way of caution.
ex.ja: 念のためもう一度いいます。

ex.en: I cautioned him against being late.
ex.ja: 彼に遅れないように注意した。

note.ja: ラテン語 cavere（用心する）から。「用心」→「注意・警告」。precaution（予防措置）も同じ。

en: The act of certifying.
The granting of a certificate.

ex.en: I've been spending a lot of time studying for IT certifications recently.
ex.ja: 最近はほとんどいつもIT関連の検定試験を受けようと勉強しています。

note.ja: certify（証明する）+ -ation。certus（確かな）+ facere（する）。「確かなものとすること」→「証明・認定」。

en: A group of people all descended from a common ancestor, in fact or belief, especially when the exact genealogies are not known.
A traditional social group of families in the Scottish Highlands having a common hereditary chieftain.

clan.ety: Borrowed from Irish clann (“offspring, children of the family”) and Scottish Gaelic clann, both from Old Irish cland, borrowed from Old Welsh plant, itself borrowed from Latin planta (“shoot, offspring”). Doublet of plant and planta.

ex.en: These figures are signs of a family or clan.
ex.ja: これらは一家族あるいは一族を表すものである。

ex.en: Clans run wild like a storm in a raging sea.
ex.ja: 猛り狂う海の嵐のように一族が激しく走る。

ex.en: Recite the names of the members of the Tokugawa clan.
ex.ja: 徳川家の系図を列挙しなさい。

note.ja: スコットランド・ゲール語 clann（子孫）から。ラテン語 planta（若枝）にさかのぼる。「同じ祖先の子孫」→「一族・氏族」。

en: A loud sound, like the crashing together of metal objects; a crash.
A skirmish, a hostile encounter.
To make a clashing sound.
To cause to make a clashing sound.

clash.ety: Of onomatopoeic origin. Compare Saterland Frisian klatskje (“to smack, slap”), West Frisian kletse, kletskje, Dutch kletsen (“to smack, slap, clash”), German Low German klattsen, klatsken (“to smack, splash”), German klatschen (“to clap, smack, slap”) and Klatsch (“a clapping sound; the din resulting from two or more things colliding”), Danish klaske (“to clash, splatter”).

ex.en: The red shoes clash with this green shirt.
ex.ja: 赤い靴にこの緑のシャツとは似合わない。

ex.en: Japanese and American interests clashed on this point.
ex.ja: 日米の利害がこの点で衝突した。

ex.en: I think the shirt clashes with the red tie.
ex.ja: このシャツはその赤いネクタイとは合わないと思うわ。

note.ja: 擬音語。武器がぶつかり合う「ガチャン」という音 →「衝突・対立」。

zh: 相處融洽的 /相处融洽的

en: Capable of working together without conflict.
Able to get along well.
Something that is compatible with something else.

compatible.ety: Inherited from Middle English compatible, fron Anglo-Norman compatible, from Medieval Latin compatibilis (“in compatibile beneficium, a benefice which could be held together with another one”), from Late Latin compator (“to suffer with”), from com- (“together”) + pati (“to suffer”); see passion.

ex.en: They are very compatible.
ex.ja: 彼ら二人はよく肌が合う。

ex.en: My tape recorder is compatible with your amplifier.
ex.ja: 私のテープレコーダーは君のアンプにもつなげられる。

ex.en: Could you convert this file into a Windows 95 compatible file and re-send it?
ex.ja: このファイルをウインドウズ９５対応のファイルに変換して再送してくれますか。

note.ja: com（共に）+ pati（感じる・耐える）+ ble。共に耐えられる →「両立できる・互換性のある」。

en: Having received a curse to be doomed to suffer eternally.
Having been sharply scolded.
A person sentenced to death.

ex.en: He must be condemned for breaking his promise.
ex.ja: 彼は約束を破ったことで非難されなければならない。

ex.en: The accused was condemned to ten years in prison.
ex.ja: 被告は懲役１０年の刑を宣告された。

ex.en: Whoever believes in him is not condemned.
ex.ja: 御子を信じるものは裁かれない。

note.ja: condemn（有罪とする）+ -ed。con（完全に）+ damnare（罰する）。damn（呪う）も同じ。

en: The form of a thing, as depending on the relative placement of the parts of a thing's shape.
The relative positions of a set of things; the way things are arranged or put together;

configuration.ety: From Middle French configuration, from Latin cōnfigūrātiō. Morphologically configure + -ation.

ex.en: It is necessary to look more carefully into the demographic configuration of this region.
ex.ja: この地域の人口構成をもっと注意深く見ていく必要がある。

ex.en: We encounter similar difficulties when we substitute rectangles for triangles in this configuration.
ex.ja: この構成において、三角形の代わりに長方形を用いても類似の困難が生ずる。

note.ja: con（共に）+ figurare（形作る）+ -ation。「全体を形づくる配置」→「構成・設定」。figure（形・数字）と同じ。

en: Without pause.

continuously.ety:
Etymology tree
English continuous
Proto-Indo-European *leyg-der.
Proto-Germanic *līkąder.
Proto-Germanic *-līkaz
Proto-Germanic *-ê
Proto-Germanic *-līkê
Proto-West Germanic *-līkē

From continuous + -ly.

ex.en: The cost of living is going up continuously.
ex.ja: 生活費はいつも上がっている。

ex.en: The north wind blew continuously all day.
ex.ja: 北風は一日中吹き続けた。

ex.en: Prices are continuously rising.
ex.ja: 物価は上がり続けている。

note.ja: continuous（絶え間ない）+ -ly。con（共に）+ tenere（保つ）。「つなぎ保つ」→「続く」。continue と同じ。

zh: 有意思的東西 /有意思的东西

en: Inquisitiveness; the tendency to ask and learn about things by asking questions, investigating, or exploring.
A unique or extraordinary object which arouses interest.

curiosity.ety: From Middle English curiosite, variant of curiouste, from Anglo-Norman curiouseté, from Latin cūriōsitātem, accusative of cūriōsitās. By surface analysis, curious + -ity. Displaced native Old English firwitt.

ex.en: A healthy curiosity is truly a fine thing.
ex.ja: 好奇心がお旺盛なのは大変に結構なことである。

ex.en: You are really full of curiosity, aren't you?
ex.ja: 君は好奇心が旺盛だね。

ex.en: I opened the box out of curiosity.
ex.ja: 好奇心から私はその箱を開けた。

note.ja: cur（注意・世話）+ ios + ity。注意を向けずにいられないこと →「好奇心・珍しいもの」。

Having the character of an explosion.
Any explosive substance.

ex.ja: 労働需要の爆発的増加がみられてきた。

ex.en: Yanni had an explosive temper.
ex.ja: ヤニーは癇癪持ちだった。

note.ja: ex（外へ）+ plos（打つ）+ ive。外へはじけ出す →「爆発性の・爆薬・爆発的な」。

en: In a fortunate manner.
It is (or was, etc) fortunate that.

ex.ja: 運の良いことに、私には話しかけることができるあなたがいるのよ。

ex.en: Fortunately, I made it to the class.
ex.ja: 幸いにも授業に間に合った。

ex.en: Fortunately he didn't die in the accident.
ex.ja: 幸運にも彼は、その事故で死ななかった。

note.ja: fortunate（幸運な）+ -ly。ラテン語 fortuna（運・運命の女神）から。fortune（財産・運）。

en: The part of a country which borders or faces another country or unsettled region.
The most advanced or recent version of something; the leading edge.
To live as pioneers on frontier territory.

frontier.ety: From Middle English frounter, from Old French fronter (whence Modern French frontière), from front.

ex.en: Many families left to make a new life on the frontier.
ex.ja: 多くの家族が新生活を築くために辺境地方に移住した。

ex.en: The soldiers headed for the frontier with caution.
ex.ja: 兵士達は警戒しながら国境に向かって進んだ。

ex.en: Many families went west to make a new life on the frontier.
ex.ja: 多くの家族が辺境で新生活を始めるため西へ行った。

note.ja: front（前面）+ -ier。「前線にある地域」→「国境地帯・辺境・最先端」。front はラテン語 frons（額）。

en: The feeling of annoyance at impossibility from resistance or inability to achieve something.
The act of frustrating, or the state, or an instance of being frustrated.

frustration.ety: From Latin frūstrātiō (“disappointment”), related to frūstrā (“in vain”). By surface analysis, frustrate + -ion.

ex.en: His anger was born of frustration.
ex.ja: 彼の怒りは欲求不満から生じた。

ex.en: Voters are taking out their frustrations at the polls.
ex.ja: 選挙民は投票によって不満をぶつけています。

ex.en: People react to the frustration in much the same way.
ex.ja: 人は欲求不満に対してほとんど同じように反応する。

note.ja: frustrate（挫折させる）+ -ation。ラテン語 frustra（むなしく）。「むなしくさせること」→「挫折・欲求不満」。

en: Pertaining to geography (or to geographics).
Determined by geography, as opposed to magnetic (i.e. North)

geographic.ety: From Latin geōgraphicus; see French géographique. By surface analysis, geography + -ic.

note.ja: geo（大地）+ graph（描く）+ ic。地理の →「地理的な」。

en: To grip; to take hold, particularly with the hand.
To understand.
Grip.
Understanding.

grasp.ety:
From Middle English graspen, grapsen, craspen (“to grope; feel around”), from Old English *grǣpsian, from Proto-West Germanic *graipisōn, from Proto-Germanic *graipisōną, from Proto-Indo-European *gʰrebʰ- (“to take, seize, rake”), the same ultimate source as grab.
Cognate with Saterland Frisian grapsje (“to grab, grasp”), German Low German grapsen (“to grab; grasp”), German grapsen and grapschen, Old English grāpian ("to touch, feel, grasp"; > Modern English grope). Compare also Swedish krafsa (“to scatch; scabble”), Norwegian krafse (“to scramble”).

ex.en: I grasped the entire structure of his argument.
ex.ja: 私は彼の議論の全体像を把握した。

ex.en: He has a good grasp of English.
ex.ja: 彼は英語をよく理解している。

ex.en: She is able to grasp the situation.
ex.ja: 彼女は情勢を把握することができる。

note.ja: 中英語 graspen（手探りする）から。grab（つかむ）と同系。「つかむ」→ 頭でつかむ →「理解する」。

en: Easy to use, useful.
Nearby, within reach.
The hand.

handy.ety: From Middle English handy, hondi (attested in personal names), alteration of earlier hendi (“handy, skillful”), from Old English *hendiġ (“skillful”) (attested in listhendiġ (“skilled in art”)), from Proto-West Germanic *handīg, *handag, *handug, from Proto-Germanic *handugaz (“handy, skillful, nimble”), from *handuz (“hand”), equivalent to hand + -y. Cognate with Saterland Frisian jäntich (“handy”), Middle Low German handich (“skillful, apt”), Middle High German handec, hendec (“manual, hand-held”), Old Norse hǫndugr (“efficient”), Gothic 𐌷𐌰𐌽𐌳𐌿𐌲𐍃 (handugs, “wise, clever”). Akin to Dutch handi

ex.en: I thought that this might come in handy.
ex.ja: これは役に立つかもしれないと思った。

ex.en: A car is a handy thing to own.
ex.ja: 車は持っていると重宝なものだ。

ex.en: I thought this might come in handy.
ex.ja: これは役に立つかもしれないと思った。

note.ja: hand（手）+ -y。「手元にある」→「便利な・手近な・器用な」。

en: Causing or likely to cause harm or damage; injurious.

harmful.ety:
From Middle English harmful, from Old English *hearmful (suggested by hearmfullīċ (“harmful; hurtful”)), equivalent to harm + -ful.
Cognate with German harmvoll, Danish harmfuld, Swedish harmfull.

ex.en: This medicine doesn't have any harmful side effects.
ex.ja: この薬には有害な副作用がありません。

ex.en: This medicine has no harmful side-effects.
ex.ja: この薬には有害な副作用がありません。

ex.en: This medicine has no harmful side effects.
ex.ja: この薬には有害な副作用がありません。

note.ja: harm（害）+ -ful。古英語 hearm（悲しみ・害）。

en: A pain or ache in the head.
A nuisance or unpleasant problem.

headache.ety: From Middle English hevedeche, from Old English hēafodeċe. By surface analysis, head + ache.

ex.en: I have a headache but no other symptoms.
ex.ja: 頭痛はありますが、他の症状はありません。

ex.en: She had a headache from lack of sleep.
ex.ja: 彼女は睡眠不足で頭痛がした。

ex.en: Whenever I drink sake, I get a headache.
ex.ja: 日本酒を飲むといつでも頭痛がする。

note.ja: head（頭）+ ache（痛み）。「頭痛」→ 悩ませるもの →「頭痛の種」。toothache、stomachache と同じ作り。

en: Something that motivates, rouses, or encourages.
A bonus or reward, often monetary, to work harder.
Inciting; encouraging or moving; rousing to action; stimulating.
Serving to kindle or set on fire.

incentive.ety: From Medieval Latin incentīvus (“that strikes up or sets the tune”), from incinō (“to strike up”), from in- (“in, on”) + canō (“to sing”) + -ive. The formation appears to have been influenced by incendō (“to set on fire”).

ex.en: The workers have no incentive to work harder.
ex.ja: 労働者たちにはもっと働こうとする刺激がなにもない。

ex.en: Promotion was an incentive to harder work.
ex.ja: 昇進がより一層働く刺激となった。

ex.en: He was incensed by their lack of incentives.
ex.ja: 彼は彼らのやる気の無さに激怒した。

note.ja: ラテン語 incentivus（調子をつける）から。in + canere（歌う）。「歌でやる気を引き出す」→「動機・誘因」。chant（歌う）も同じ canere。

en: The state of being mad; insanity; mental disease.
The state of being angry.

madness.ety: From Middle English madnes, madnesse; equivalent to mad + -ness.

ex.en: What he did was nothing less than madness.
ex.ja: 彼がしたことは狂気の沙汰としか言いようがなかった。

ex.en: It's the height of madness to say so.
ex.ja: そんなことを言うのは狂気のさただ。

ex.en: His conduct was nothing short of madness.
ex.ja: 彼の行為はまさしく狂気の沙汰だった。

note.ja: mad（狂った）+ -ness。「狂気・ばかげたこと」。

en: An official or authoritative command; an order or injunction; a commission; a judicial precept; an authorization.
The order or authority to do something, as granted to a politician by the electorate.
To (officially) require someone to do something or act in a certain way, to give them the authority to do so; to command.
To make mandatory.

mandate.ety:
First attested in 1521; borrowed from Latin mandātum (“a charge, order, command, commission, injunction”), substantivized from the neuter forms of mandātus, perfect passive participle of mandō (“to commit to one's charge, order, command, commission, literally to put into one's hands”) (see -ate (noun-forming suffix)), from manus (“hand”) + -dere (“to put”).
Sense 3 in Canadian English is likely a semantic loan from French mandat.

note.ja: ラテン語 mandare（手に委ねる・命じる）から。manus（手）+ dare（与える）。「手に預ける」→「委任・権限・命令」。command、demand も同じ。

en: A comic originating in Japan.
An artistic style heavily used in, and associated with, Japanese comics, and that has also been adopted by a comparatively low number of …

Borrowed from Japanese 漫画(まんが) (manga), from Middle Chinese 漫 (MC manH, “free, unrestrained”) + 畫 (MC hweaH|hweak, “drawing”). Compare Mandarin 漫畫／漫画 (mànhuà), Korean 만화 (漫畵／漫畫, manhwa). After an 1814 book by Katsushika Hokusai. Doublet of manhua and manhwa.

ex.en: I learned everything important in life from mangas.
ex.ja: 人生で大切なことはすべて漫画から学んだ。

ex.en: This manga is pretty popular in China.
ex.ja: この漫画は中国でとても人気がある。

ex.en: The kid has a lot of mangas.
ex.ja: その子は漫画をいっぱい持ってるんだ。

note.ja: 日本語「漫画」がそのまま英語になった語。

ex.ja: 両社の合併の知らせがきのう突然伝わった。

ex.ja: その合併は１対１で行われた。

ex.ja: 今まで一度もポーカーをやったことがないって、本当？

ex.ja: 彼はポーカーがとても上手だ。

note.ja: poke（つつく）+ -er。「火をつつく棒」→「火かき棒」。トランプのポーカーは別の語源とされる。

en: The act or practice of robbing.
The offense of taking or attempting to take the property of another by force or threat of force.

From Middle English robberie, robry, roberie, from Old French roberie, from the verb rober (“to steal; to pillage”) + -ie. Ultimately from unattested Frankish *raubōn. By surface analysis, rob + -ery. Compare Dutch roverij (“robbery”), Norwegian Bokmål røveri (“

ex.en: He has something to do with the robbery.
ex.ja: 彼はその強盗事件と関係がある。

ex.en: He was sent to jail for the robbery.
ex.ja: 彼は強盗の罪で刑務所に送られた。

ex.en: Bank robbery will cost you ten years in prison.
ex.ja: 銀行強盗すると懲役１０年食らうぞ。

note.ja: rob（奪う）+ -ery。rob は古フランス語 rober から、ゲルマン系で「服をはぎ取る」。robe（長い衣服：はぎ取った戦利品）と同じ語源。

en: An act of rubbing.
A difficulty or problem.
To move (one object) while maintaining contact with another object over some area, with pressure and friction.
To be rubbed against something.

rub.ety:
Inherited from Middle English rubben, of unknown origin; possibly ultimately from Proto-Germanic *rubbōną, a hypothetical variant of *ruppōną (“to tear (off), rip; to wear away, rub”), related to *reufaną (“to tear”) (> English reave). If so, a doublet of rip.
Cognate with Saterland Frisian rubje (“to rub, scrape”), German Low German rubben (“to rub”), Low German rubblig (“rough, uneven”), Dutch robben, rubben (“to rub smooth; scrape; scrub”), Danish rubbe (“to rub, scrub”), Icelandic and Norwegian rubba (“to scrape”).
More at reave.
Compare typologically Latin fricō < friō < Proto-Indo-Europe

ex.en: Everything he says rubs me the wrong way.
ex.ja: 彼の言うことすべてが、私の神経を逆なでするのです。

ex.en: I sure rubbed your nose in shit.
ex.ja: お前の鼻をクソに擦りつけてやった。

ex.en: Never rub your eyes with dirty hands.
ex.ja: 汚れた手で目をこすってはいけません。

note.ja: 中英語 rubben から。北欧系とされる。「こする」。rubber（ゴム：鉛筆の跡をこすって消すもの）。

en: A willow.
Any tree that resembles a willow.
To make a sudden attack (e.g. on an enemy from a defended position).
To set out on an excursion; venture; depart (often followed by "forth").

sally.ety: From Middle English saly, from Old English saliġ, sealh (“willow”). More at sallow.

ex.en: Sally and I work in the same office.
ex.ja: サリーは職場の仲間です。

ex.en: Sally gave me a good piece of information.
ex.ja: サリーは私に良い情報を１つ教えてくれた。

ex.en: Sally made her brother clean the bathroom.
ex.ja: サリーは弟にバスルームを掃除させた。

note.ja: フランス語 saillie（飛び出し）から。ラテン語 salire（跳ぶ）。「城から飛び出す攻撃」→「出撃」、言葉が飛び出す →「気のきいた言葉」。

en: Dispersed, spread apart into disunited units.
Seemingly randomly distributed.

ex.en: Broken glass lay scattered all over the road.
ex.ja: ガラスの破片が、道路一面に散らばってたよ。

ex.en: The sudden noise scattered the birds.
ex.ja: 突然の物音に鳥たちは散り散りに飛び去った。

ex.en: The wind scattered the leaves about.
ex.ja: 風が葉を吹き散らした。

note.ja: scatter（まき散らす）+ -ed。shatter（粉々にする）と同系。「散らばった」→「まばらな」。

en: A person sent out to gather and bring back information; especially, one employed in war to gain information about the enemy and ground.
An act of scouting or reconnoitering.
To explore a wide terrain, as if on a search.
To observe, watch, or look for, as a scout; to follow for the purpose of observation, as a scout.

From Middle English scout, scoult, from Old French escoute (“action of listening”), verbal noun from escouter (“to listen, heed”), from Latin auscultō (“to listen”). The verb comes from the noun.

ex.en: When did you become a Boy Scout?
ex.ja: ボーイスカウトになったのはいつぐらい？

ex.en: The boy scouts went from door to door selling what they had made.
ex.ja: ボーイスカウトたちは自分たちの作った物を一軒一軒売ってまわった。

ex.en: I was scouted by a model agency while walking around Shibuya.
ex.ja: 渋谷を歩いていてモデルエージェンシーにスカウトされた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 escouter（聞く）から。ラテン語 auscultare（耳を傾ける）。「耳をすませて偵察する人」→「偵察兵」→ 人材を探す →「スカウト」。

en: The quality of being sexual; that which is characterized or distinguished by sex.
Sexual activity; concern with, or interest in, sexual activity.

sexuality.ety:

en: A blow, especially one given with the open hand, or with something broad and flat.
A sharp percussive sound like that produced by such a blow.
To strike someone, typically with an open hand, often on the face.
To cause something to strike soundly.
Exactly, precisely

slap.ety: From Middle English slappen, of uncertain origin, possibly imitative. Compare Low German Slappe (“slap”), whence also German Schlappe (“defeat”). Compare also Italian sleppa (“slap”).

ex.ja: だからって・・・なにもひっぱたくことないじゃないか。

ex.en: Can I slap you? I can't contain myself.
ex.ja: 引っ叩いていい？腹の虫が治まらないんだけど。

note.ja: 擬音語。「パチン」と平手でたたく音から。

en: Beefsteak: a slice of beef, broiled or cut for broiling.
A relatively large, thick slice or slab cut from another animal, a vegetable, etc.
To cook (something, especially fish) like or as a steak.

steak.ety:
From Middle English steike, from Old Norse steik (“roast; meat roasted on a stick”). The verb is either from the noun or from steikja (“to roast”).
The modern pronunciation shows an irregular change of Early Modern English /ɛː/ to /eɪ/ in the standard language; contrast this with the development of other words such as speak and wreak.

ex.en: He ate up the steak and ordered another.
ex.ja: 彼はそのステーキを平らげてもう１つ注文した。

ex.en: Would you like to have steak for dinner?
ex.ja: 夜ご飯にステーキはどうですか？

ex.en: Steak and red wine make a good combination.
ex.ja: ステーキと赤ワインはいい取り合わせだ。

note.ja: 北欧語 steik（焼いた肉）から。stick（棒）と同系で「串に刺して焼く」。

en: An act of following in sequence.
A sequence of things in order.

succession.ety: Inherited from Middle English [Term?], from Old French succession, from Latin successiō (noun).

ex.en: They won the Japan Cup three years in succession.
ex.ja: 彼らは３年連続してジャパン・カップに優勝した。

ex.en: After a succession of warm days, the weather became cold.
ex.ja: 暖かい日が連続した後、天候は寒くなった。

ex.en: He came to the throne by succession.
ex.ja: 彼は世襲によって王位についた。

note.ja: suc（次に）+ cess（進む）+ ion。次々に続くこと →「連続・継承」。

en: A person who is authorized to supervise, direct or administer something.
A police officer rank, positioned above chief inspector, and below chief superintendent.
Overseeing; superintending.

superintendent.ety: From Ecclesiastical Latin superintendens, a calque of Ancient Greek ἐπίσκοπος (epískopos); thence being distantly related to English bishop.

note.ja: super（上から）+ intendere（気を配る）+ -ent。「上から気を配る人」→「監督者・管理者」。intend と同じ。

en: The act of suspecting something or someone, especially of something wrong.
The condition of being suspected.

suspicion.ety: From Middle English suspecioun, borrowed from Latin suspīciō, suspīciōnem, from suspicere, from sub- (“up to”) with specere (“to look at”). Perhaps partly through the influence of Old French sospeçon (or rather the Anglo-Norman form suspecioun). Equivalent to suspect + -ion.

ex.en: He fell under the suspicion of the police.
ex.ja: 彼は警察の嫌疑を受けた。

ex.en: Her unusual behavior gave rise to our suspicions.
ex.ja: 彼女の異常な行動が私たちの疑いを引き起こした。

ex.en: I have a suspicion about his death.
ex.ja: 私は彼の死に対して疑いを持っている。

note.ja: sub（下から）+ specere（見る）+ -ion。「下から（疑いの目で）見ること」→「疑い」。suspect、inspect も同じ specere。

en: To clean (a surface) by means of a stroking motion of a broom or brush.
To move through a (horizontal) arc or similar long stroke.
A single action of sweeping.
The person who steers a dragon boat.

sweep.ety: From Middle English swepen, from Proto-West Germanic *swaipijan (unattested in Old English), from Proto-Germanic *swaipijaną. Cognate with Early Modern West Frisian swiepe (“whip, cleanse, sweep”), from Old Frisian swēpa, suepa (“sweep”). More distantly related to Old Norse sveipa (whence Swedish svepa). See also swoop.

ex.en: Did you order the room to be swept?
ex.ja: 部屋を掃除するように命じましたか。

ex.en: A shadow of anxiety swept across her face.
ex.ja: 不安の影が彼女の顔をさっとよぎった。

ex.en: The children were assigned to sweep the room.
ex.ja: 子供たちは部屋の掃除を割り当てられた。

note.ja: 古英語 swāpan（掃く）から。swoop（急降下する）と同系。「さっと払う」→「掃く・一掃する」。

A psychotherapist specifically.

en: After that time, from then on; thenceforth.
After that (the thing aforementioned).
Synonym of hereafter (“future existence or state”).
Synonym of hereafter (“existence after death”).

thereafter.ety: From Middle English therafter, theraftir, þerefter, þerafter, þeræfter, from Old English þǣræfter (“after that; thereafter”), equivalent to there + after. Cognate with Saterland Frisian deerätter (“thereafter”), West Frisian dêrefter (“behind that; thereafter”), Dutch daarachter (“behind that; thereafter”), German Low German daarachter (“behind that”), Danish derefter (“thereafter”), Swedish därefter (“thereafter”).

ex.en: Thereafter we heard no more from him.
ex.ja: その後彼からは便りが無かった。

ex.en: Thereafter, he was gradually promoted until he became company president.
ex.ja: 彼はその後、累進して社長にまで進んだ。

note.ja: there（そこ）+ after（後に）。「その後」。thereby、therefore と同じ作り。

en: Painstaking and careful not to miss or omit any detail.
Utter; complete; absolute.

thorough.ety: From Middle English thoruȝ, þoruȝ, from Old English þuruh, a byform of Old English þurh, whence comes English through. The adjective derives from the preposition and adverb. The word developed a syllabic form in cases where the word was fully stressed: when it was used as an adverb, adjective, or noun, and less commonly when used as a preposition.

ex.en: He made a thorough analysis of the problem.
ex.ja: 彼はその問題を徹底的に分析した。

ex.en: The theory is based on thorough research.
ex.ja: その理論は周到な研究に基づいている。

ex.en: A thorough investigation is now in progress.
ex.ja: 詳しい調査は今進行中です。

note.ja: through（通して）の古い形。「端から端まで通した」→「徹底的な・完全な」。

en: The training or instruction provided by a teacher or tutor.
Paid private classes taken outside of formal education; tutoring. (also used attributively)

tuition.ety: From Anglo-Norman tuycioun, from Old French tuicion, from Latin tuitiō (“guard, protection, defense”), from tuēri (“to watch, guard, see, observe”). Compare intuition, tutor.

ex.en: I got a grant for my tuition.
ex.ja: 奨学金が交付された。

ex.en: I am working to save for my college tuition.
ex.ja: 大学の授業料をためるために働いています。

ex.en: They announced an increase in tuition fees.
ex.ja: 学校は授業料の値上げを発表した。

note.ja: ラテン語 tueri（見守る）から。「見守って教えること」→「指導」→ その費用 →「授業料」。tutor（家庭教師）も同じ。

en: An abnormal growth; differential diagnosis includes abscess, metaplasia, and neoplasia.

tumor.ety: From Middle English tumour, from Old French tumour, from Latin tumor (“swelling”), from tumeō (“bulge, swell”, verb), from Proto-Italic *tumēō, from Proto-Indo-European *tewh₂- (“to swell”). Related to English thumb.

ex.en: Tom had a brain tumor.
ex.ja: トムには脳腫瘍があった。

ex.en: I got a stomach tumor and had to have it operated on.
ex.ja: 胃に腫瘍ができたので切ってもらった。

ex.en: I have a tumor.
ex.ja: 私、腫瘍があるんだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 tumere（腫れる）から。「腫れ」→「腫瘍」。

en: The sale of products, often in large quantities, to retailers or other merchants.
Of or relating to sale in large quantities, for resale.
Extensive, indiscriminate, all-encompassing; blanket.
In bulk or large quantity.
Indiscriminately.
To sell at wholesale.

ex.en: Wholesale prices are basically flat.
ex.ja: 卸売物価は基本的に安定している。

ex.en: A retail merchant buys wholesale and sells retail.
ex.ja: 小売商人は卸しで仕入れて小売りで売る。

ex.en: This morning, Mr Yamaha bought 30 kilos of walnuts wholesale.
ex.ja: 今朝、山羽さんが卸で胡桃を３０キロ買いました。

note.ja: whole（全体）+ sale（販売）。「まとめて全部売る」→「卸売り」→「大規模な」。

en: To apportion out, distribute.
To manage or supervise the conduct, performance or execution of; to govern or regulate the parameters for the conduct, performance or exe…

administer.ety: From Middle English administren, from Old French aminister, from Latin administrare (“to manage, execute”), from ad (“to”) + ministrare (“to attend, serve”), from minister (“servant”); see minister.

ex.en: The mayor administers the affairs of the city.
ex.ja: 市長は市政を司る。

ex.en: The Secretary of State administers foreign affairs.
ex.ja: 国務長官は対外関係を統括する。

ex.en: A new principal is administering the school.
ex.ja: 新しい校長が学校を管理運営している。

note.ja: ad（〜に）+ ministrare（仕える）。「人のために仕える」→「管理する・運営する・（薬を）投与する」。minister（大臣：仕える者）と同じ。

en: Large projectile weapons, in modern usage usually large guns, but also rocket artillery.
An army unit that uses such weapons, or a military formation using projectile weapons, such as archers.

artillery.ety: From Middle English artillerie, from Old French artillerie (“collection of military engines, crossbows, lances etc.”), from artillier (“to equip, provide with contraptions”), alteration of atiller (“to arrange, adjust, put on clothes or, especially, pieces of armour”) (influenced by art), itself from Vulgar Latin *apticlō < **apticulō, from Latin aptō (“to make capable”).

note.ja: 古フランス語 artillerie（兵器）から。art（技術）と関係するとされる。「戦の道具」→「大砲・砲兵隊」。

en: A type of coarse cloth, woven from hemp (traditionally) or from cotton and polyesters, useful for making sails, tents, and overcoats or a…
A piece of such cloth stretched across a frame on which one may paint an artwork.
To cover (an area or object) with canvas.

canvas.ety: From Middle English canevas, from Anglo-Norman, from Old Northern French canevas (compare Old French chanevas, chenevas) from a root derived from Latin cannabis, from Ancient Greek κάνναβις (kánnabis). Compare French canevas, resulting from a blend of the Old French and a Picard dialect word, itself from Old Northern French. Doublet of cannabis and hemp.

ex.en: This world is but canvas to our imaginations.
ex.ja: この世は我々の想像力にとっての画布そのものである。

ex.en: He swept his brush across the canvas.
ex.ja: 彼は絵筆をカンバスにさっと走らせた。

ex.en: Oil on canvas can never paint a petal so delicate.
ex.ja: キャンバスのオイルはとても微細な花びらを描けない。

note.ja: ラテン語 cannabis（麻）から。「麻で織った布」→「帆布」→ 絵を描く布 →「キャンバス」。

en: A valley, especially a long, narrow, steep valley, cut in rock by a river.
Of water, liquid, or another substance, to flow in or into a canyon.

canyon.ety: Borrowed from Spanish cañón. Doublet of cannon.

ex.en: The Grand Canyon is one of the most popular places in the USA.
ex.ja: グランド・キャニオンはアメリカ有数の人気スポットだ。

ex.en: The Grand Canyon is the number one tourist attraction in America.
ex.ja: グランド・キャニオンはアメリカで一番人気のある観光スポットです。

note.ja: スペイン語 cañón（筒・管）から。caña（葦）+ 拡大の -ón。「大きな管のような谷」→「峡谷」。cannon と同系。

en: The soft skin on each side of the face, below the eyes; the outer surface of the sides of the oral cavity.
The lower part of the buttocks that is often exposed beneath very brief underwear, swimwear, or extremely short shorts.
To be impudent towards.
To pull a horse's head back toward the saddle using the cheek strap of the bridle.

cheek.ety:
From Middle English cheeke, cheke, cheoke, choke, from Old English ċēce, ċēace, ċēoce (“cheek; jaw”), from Proto-West Germanic *kākā, *keukā (“jaw, cheek”), from Proto-Germanic *kēkǭ, *keukǭ (“jaw; palate; pharynx”), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *ǵyewh₁- (“to chew”).
Cognate with Saterland Frisian Sooke (“cheek”), West Frisian tsjeak (“jaw”), Dutch kaak (“jaw; cheek”), Swedish käke (“jaw; jowl”), Norwegian kjake (“jaw”), Old Norse kók (“mouth; gullet”).

ex.en: Tom gave Mary a kiss on both cheeks.
ex.ja: トムはメアリーの両頬にキスをした。

ex.en: Mary gave me a kiss on the cheek.
ex.ja: メアリーがほっぺにちゅってしてくれた。

ex.en: It was only a kiss on the cheek.
ex.ja: ほっぺにキスしただけだろ。

note.ja: 古英語 cēace（あご・頬）から。「頬」→ 頬をふくらませて言う生意気 →「生意気（なことば）」。

en: Of or relating to a circle.
In the shape of, or moving in, a circle.
An advertisement, directive or notice intended for mass circulation.
A shuttle bus with a circular route.
To distribute circulars to or at.
To extend in a circular direction.

circular.ety: From Middle English circuler, circuleer, circulere, from Old French circulier (French circulaire), from Late Latin circularis, from Latin circulus, diminutive of circus (“ring”). By surface analysis, circle + -ar.

ex.ja: ポストに回覧板入れといたよ。

ex.ja: ポストに回覧板入れといたよ。

ex.en: I put the circular in the letter box.
ex.ja: ポストに回覧板入れといたよ。

note.ja: circle（円）+ -ar。ラテン語 circulus（小さな輪）。「円形の」→ 人々の間を回る →「回覧・ちらし」。

en: The act of moving in a circle, or in a course which brings the moving body to the place where its motion began.
The act of passing from place to place or person to person; free diffusion; transmission.

circulation.ety: From Middle English circulacioun, from Latin circulatio. Morphologically circulate + -ion.

ex.ja: 彼はこのごろ影を潜めてる。

ex.en: This paper has a large circulation.
ex.ja: この新聞は購読者が多い。

ex.en: This newspaper has a large circulation.
ex.ja: この新聞は発行部数が多い。

note.ja: circulate（循環する）+ -ation。「輪になって回ること」→「循環・流通・発行部数」。

The distance between two moving objects, especially between parts of a machine

The appearance of a meaningful connection between events when there is none.

coincidence.ety: From Middle French coincidence (French coïncidence). By surface analysis, coincide + -ence.

ex.ja: 不思議な巡り合わせで私達はばったり再会した。

en: An entertainer who performs in a humorous manner, especially by telling jokes.
Any person who is humorous or amusing, either characteristically or on a particular occasion.

comedian.ety: From French comédien, from comédie + -ien, from Old French comedie, from Latin cōmoedia, from Ancient Greek κωμῳδία (kōmōidía). By surface analysis, comed(y) + -ian.

ex.ja: 彼女は歌手と言うよりはコメディアンだ。

ex.en: That comedian is very funny.
ex.ja: あの喜劇役者は大変こっけいだ。

ex.en: Comedians base their jokes on tragic situations like violent death or serious accidents.
ex.ja: コメディアンは無惨な死や大事故といった悲劇的状況を冗談のネタにしている。

note.ja: comedy（喜劇）+ -ian。ギリシャ語 kōmōidia、kōmos（お祭り騒ぎ）+ aoidos（歌い手）。

en: The ethical or moral sense of right and wrong, chiefly as it affects a person’s own behaviour and forms their attitude to their past acti…
A personification of the moral sense of right and wrong, usually in the form of a person, a being or merely a voice that gives moral less…

conscience.ety: From Middle English conscience, from Old French conscience, from Latin conscientia (“knowledge within oneself”) (a calque of Ancient Greek σῠνείδησῐς (sŭneídēsĭs)), from consciens, present participle of conscire (“to know, to be conscious (of wrong)”), from com- (“together”) + scire (“to know”).

ex.ja: あなたは自分の良心に従って行動すべきだ。

ex.ja: 私はその事ではやましく思っている。

ex.en: Tom said that his conscience is clear.
ex.ja: トムは自分の心が潔白だと言っていた。

ex.ja: 空には無数の星が見えた。

ex.en: I've been to Boston countless times.
ex.ja: ボストンには何回か行ったことがあります。

note.ja: count（数える）+ -less（〜がない）。「数えられない」→「無数の」。

en: One of a family of dishes originating from Indian cuisine, flavored by a spiced sauce.
A spiced sauce or relish, especially one flavored with curry powder.
To cook or season with curry powder.

curry.ety:
Etymology tree
Tamil கறி (kaṟi)bor.
English currey
Middle English curyinflu.
English curry
1747 (as currey, first published recipe for the dish in English), from Tamil கறி (kaṟi), influenced by existing Middle English cury (“cooking”), from Middle French cuyre (“to cook”) (whence also cuisine), from Vulgar Latin cocere, from Latin coquere.
Earlier cury found in 1390 cookbook Forme of Cury (Forms of Cooking) by court chefs of Richard II of England.

ex.en: I think I'll make curry for dinner tonight.
ex.ja: 今日の夕飯はカレーを作ろうと思います。

ex.en: I'd like to eat curry rice for dinner.
ex.ja: 今夜はカレーが食べたいな。

ex.en: I had curry and rice last night.
ex.ja: 昨夜カレーを食べた。

note.ja: タミル語 kari（ソース・味つけ）から。

en: No longer alive; dead.
Belonging to the dead.
Synonym of dead (“those who have died”).
One who has died. In property law, the alternate term decedent is generally used in US English. In criminal law, “the deceased” refers to…

deceased.ety: From decease + -ed, from Middle English deceas via Old French [Term?], from Latin dēcessus (“departure”), equivalent to dēced-, variation of dēcēdō, dēcēdere (“to go away”).

ex.en: I often think about my deceased mother.
ex.ja: 私はしばしば亡くなった母のことを考える。

ex.en: She has a claim on her deceased husband's estate.
ex.ja: 彼女は死んだ夫の財産の相続権をもっている。

ex.en: The deceased was eighty years old.
ex.ja: 故人は８０歳であった。

note.ja: decease（死亡）+ -ed。de（離れて）+ cedere（行く）。「この世から去った」→「亡くなった」。

en: The act of detaining or the state of being detained; hindrance.
Confinement of a prisoner awaiting trial.

detention.ety: Borrowed from Middle French détention, from Latin detentio, detentionem. Equivalent to detain + -tion.

ex.en: Tom was given detention for talking during class.
ex.ja: トムは授業中おしゃべりをしていたので居残りさせられた。

ex.en: I escaped from the detention center.
ex.ja: 私は収容所から脱走した。

note.ja: de（離れて）+ tent（保つ）+ ion。引き離して留めておくこと →「拘留・居残り」。

en: A male duck (bird).

drake.ety:
