From Middle English drake (“male duck, drake”), either from Old English *draca, *andraca (“male duck, drake”) or from Middle Low German drâke, andrâke, from Proto-West Germanic *anadrekō (“drake”, literally “duck l

ex.en: Perry decided to gain information from Drake.
ex.ja: ペリーはドレークから情報をもらうことにした。

ex.en: Drake earns his living by working for the lawyer.
ex.ja: ドレークは弁護士のために働くことで暮らしを立てている。

note.ja: 古英語に由来するゲルマン系の語。「雄のカモ」。duck は雌・総称。

en: To keep up, impose or bring into effect something, not necessarily by force.
To apply a rule or enforcement action to a person or user account.

enforce.ety: From Middle English enforcen, from Old French enforcier, from Late Latin infortiāre, from in- + fortis (“strong”).

ex.en: The government must enforce the law immediately.
ex.ja: 政府は法律を施行しなければならない。

ex.en: The new law was enforced on the people of the island.
ex.ja: その島の住民に新しい法律が施行された。

ex.en: The law was enforced immediately.
ex.ja: その法律は直ちに実施された。

note.ja: en（〜にする）+ forc（力）+ e。力をもたせる →「（法律などを）施行する・強いる」。

en: Very specific, clear, or detailed.
Containing material (e.g. language or film footage) that might be deemed offensive or graphic through clear and direct expressions.
The final few words of a text.

explicit.ety: Borrowed from French explicite, from Latin explicitus (“disentangled, easy”), variant of explicātus.

ex.en: I gave you explicit instructions not to touch anything.
ex.ja: 私はあなたに何にも触るなとはっきりと指示しました。

ex.en: He was explicit on the point.
ex.ja: 彼はその点をはっきり述べた。

ex.en: He was explicit in his instruction.
ex.ja: 彼の指示は明白だった。

note.ja: ex（外へ）+ plic（折る）+ it。折りたたまれたものを外へ広げた →「明白な・露骨な」。implicit（中に折り込まれた→暗黙の）と対。

en: In an explicit manner.

explicitly.ety:
Etymology tree
English explicit
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English explicitly
From explicit + -ly.

note.ja: explicit（明確な）+ -ly。ex（外へ）+ plicare（たたむ・折る）。「たたまれたものを広げた」→「はっきりと」。反対は implicit（中に折り込まれた → 暗黙の）。

en: Influenza.
Stomach flu.

ex.en: Did you receive your flu shot this season?
ex.ja: 今シーズン、インフルエンザの予防接種は受けましたか？

ex.en: There's a lot of flu going around now.
ex.ja: 今インフルエンザが流行ってます。

ex.en: I was in bed with the flu.
ex.ja: 私はインフルエンザで寝てたんです。

note.ja: influenza の短縮形。イタリア語 influenza（星の影響）から。昔、流行病は天体の影響と考えられた。influence と同じ。

en: Not allowed; specifically disallowed.

forbidden.ety: Past participle of the verb forbid. Doublet of verboten. Compare German verboten, Dutch verboden, Swedish förbjuden, and West Frisian ferbean.

ex.en: It is forbidden for you to touch that switch.
ex.ja: 絶対にそのスイッチに触ってはいけない。

ex.en: I am forbidden to use this telephone.
ex.ja: 私はこの電話を使うのを禁じられている。

ex.en: Alcohol is forbidden in many Muslim countries.
ex.ja: アルコールは多くのイスラム教国で禁じられています。

note.ja: forbid（禁じる）の過去分詞。for（反対に）+ bid（命じる）。「しないよう命じる」→「禁じられた」。

en: A part of a whole, especially a comparatively small part.
A ratio of two numbers (numerator and denominator), usually written one above the other and separated by a horizontal bar called the vinc…
To divide or break into fractions.
To fractionate.

fraction.ety:
Etymology tree
Old French fraccionbor.
Middle English fraccioun
English fraction
From Middle English fraccioun (“a breaking”), from Anglo-Norman, Old French fraccion, from Medieval Latin fractio (“a fragment, portion”), from earlier Latin fractio (“a breaking, a breaking into pieces”), from fractus, past participle of frangere (“to break”) (whence English frangible), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰreg- (English break). Doublet of frazione.

ex.en: The fraction b/a means b times 1/a.
ex.ja: 分数b/aは1/aをb倍した数を意味する。

ex.en: He did it in only a fraction of a second.
ex.ja: 彼は１秒のほんの何分の１かでそれをした。

ex.en: Time is a certain fraction of eternity.
ex.ja: 時とは、永遠の一部分である。

note.ja: fract（壊す）+ ion。壊して分けたもの →「分数・ほんの一部」。fragile（壊れやすい）も同じ。

en: Soldiers who fight on foot (on land), as opposed to cavalry and other mounted units, regardless of external transport (e.g. airborne).
The part of an army consisting of infantry soldiers, especially opposed to mounted and technical troops.

infantry.ety: From Middle French infanterie, from older Italian, possibly from Spanish infantería (“foot soldiers, force composed of those too inexperienced or low in rank for cavalry”), from infante (“foot soldier”), originally "a youth", either way from Latin īnfāns (“child”); see there for more.

ex.en: The infantry soldier is only a pawn in the game of war.
ex.ja: 戦争の際には歩兵は取るに足らないものだ。

en: Constituting a whole together with other parts or factors; not omittable or removable.
Of, pertaining to, or being an integer.
One of the two fundamental operations of calculus (the other being differentiation), whereby a function's displacement, area, volume, or …
Any of several analytic formalizations of this operation: the Riemann integral, the Lebesgue integral, etc.

integral.ety: Borrowed from Middle French integral, from Medieval Latin integrālis, from Latin integer (“entire”); see integer.

note.ja: ラテン語 integer（触れられていない→完全な）から。in（否定）+ teg（触れる）。欠けていない →「不可欠な・完全な」。

en: In a light manner.

lightly.ety: From Middle English lyghtly, liȝtliche, lihtliche, from Old English lēohtlīċe, equivalent to light + -ly.

ex.en: I dress lightly all the time.
ex.ja: 私はいつも薄着です。

ex.en: He took the reality of the situation lightly and failed.
ex.ja: 彼はその事実を軽く見て失敗した。

ex.en: If you go out so lightly dressed, you'll catch a cold.
ex.ja: そんな薄着で外出たら風邪引くよ。

note.ja: light（軽い）+ -ly。「軽く・軽々しく・そっと」。

en: A metamorphic rock of crystalline limestone.
A small ball used in games, originally of marble but now usually of glass or ceramic.
To cause (something to have) the streaked or swirled appearance of certain types of marble, for example by mixing viscous ingredients inc…
To get or have the streaked or swirled appearance of certain types of marble, for example due to the incomplete mixing of viscous ingredi…
Made of, or resembling, marble.
Cold; hard; unfeeling.

marble.ety: Inherited from Middle English marble, marbre; from Anglo-Norman and Old French marbre, from Latin marmor, from Ancient Greek μάρμαρος (mármaros), perhaps related to μαρμάρεος (marmáreos, “gleaming”). The forms from French displaced Old English marma, which had previously been borrowed from Latin.

ex.en: Her hands felt as cold as marble.
ex.ja: 彼女の手は冷たい大理石のような感じがした。

ex.en: He must have lost his marbles.
ex.ja: 彼はいかれちまったに違いない。

ex.en: The desk is made of marble.
ex.ja: その机は大理石でできてます。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 marmaros（輝く石）から。「大理石」→ 大理石で作った小さな玉 →「ビー玉」。

en: To change (or to be changed) from a solid state to a liquid state, usually by a gradual heat.
To dissolve, disperse, vanish.
Molten material, the product of melting.
The transition of matter from a solid state to a liquid state.

melt.ety: From Middle English melten, from a merger of Old English meltan (intransitive) and mieltan (transitive), both meaning “to melt, digest,” from Proto-West Germanic *meltan and *maltijan, from Proto-Germanic *meltaną and *maltijaną, both from Proto-Indo-European *(s)meld- (“melt”). Cognate with Icelandic melta (“to digest”).

ex.en: I think that the snow will melt soon.
ex.ja: 雪はすぐに解けると思いますよ。

ex.en: Ice turns back into water when it melts.
ex.ja: 氷は解けると水に戻る。

ex.en: When a solid melts, it becomes liquid.
ex.ja: 固体が解けると液体になる。

note.ja: 古英語 meltan（溶ける）から。smelt（精錬する）、malt（麦芽）と同系。「溶ける」→ 心が溶ける →「和らぐ」。

en: A solemn pledge or promise that invokes a deity, a ruler, or another entity (not necessarily present) to attest the truth of a statement …
A statement or promise which is strengthened (affirmed) by such a pledge.

oath.ety:
From Middle English ooth, oth, ath, from Old English āþ (“oath”), from Proto-West Germanic *aiþ (“oath”), from Proto-Germanic *aiþaz (“oath”).
Cognate with Scots aith, athe (“oath”), North Frisian ith, iss (“oath”), Saterland Frisian Eed (“oath”), West Frisian eed (“oath”), Dutch eed (“oath”), German Eid (“oath”), Swedish ed (“oath”), Icelandic eið (“oath”), Latin ūtor (“make use of, employ, avail”, verb), Old Irish óeth (“oath”).

ex.en: She gave her oath that she would not drink.
ex.ja: 彼女は酒をやめると誓った。

ex.en: I will read the athletes' oath at sports day.
ex.ja: 僕、運動会で選手宣誓するんだ。

ex.en: He said under oath that he was born in Italy.
ex.ja: 彼は出生地は確かにイタリアだと誓った。

note.ja: 古英語 āth（誓い）から。ドイツ語 Eid と同じゲルマン系の語。

en: A person who loves and zealously supports and defends their country.

patriot.ety: From Middle French patriote, from Late Latin patriōta (“fellow countryman”) from the Ancient Greek πατριώτης (patriṓtēs, “of the same country”), from πατρίς (patrís, “father land", "country”), from πατήρ (patḗr, “father”).

ex.en: The patriots stood up for the rights of their nation.
ex.ja: 愛国者達は国民の権利を擁護した。

ex.en: No man can be a patriot on an empty stomach.
ex.ja: 何人も空の胃の腑では愛国者たり得ない。

ex.en: The patriot sticks to his moral principles.
ex.ja: その愛国者は自分の道徳的な信条を曲げない。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 patriotes（同じ祖国の人）から。patr（父）。父祖の国を愛する人 →「愛国者」。

en: Urine.
An act of urination.
To urinate.
To urinate on oneself.

pee.ety: The initial letter of piss. Compare eff.

ex.en: With practice, even girls can pee standing up.
ex.ja: 訓練すれば、女の子だって立っておしっこできます。

ex.en: You scared me so much I peed myself a little.
ex.ja: ビックリしすぎてちょっと漏れちゃった…。

ex.en: Can I go to the bathroom? I need to pee.
ex.ja: トイレに行ってもいい？おしっこしたい。

note.ja: piss の頭文字 p を発音した婉曲語。

en: A soft cushion used to support the head in bed.
Any similar head support used for sleep, such as a neck pillow or a hard porcelain pillow.
To rest as on a pillow.

pillow.ety:
From Middle English pilwe, from Old English pyle, pylu (“pillow”), from Proto-West Germanic *pulwī (“pillow”), from Latin pulvīnus (“cushion”), derived from pulvis (“dust”), for the filler of a pillow. Doublet of pulvinus.
Cognate with Saterland Frisian Peel (“pillow”), Alemannic German Pfulme (“pillow”), Dutch peluw (“a long, narrow pillow”), German Pfühl (“a big and soft pillow”), German Low German Pöhl (“pad, pillow, cushion”).

ex.en: She laid her head down on the pillow.
ex.ja: 彼女は頭を枕にのせた。

ex.en: Tom decided to try sleeping without a pillow.
ex.ja: トムは枕なしで眠ろうと決めた。

ex.en: He laid his head on the pillow.
ex.ja: 彼は枕に頭を横たえた。

note.ja: ラテン語 pulvinus（クッション）から古英語に入った語。

en: A statement of what will happen in the future.
A probability estimation based on statistical methods.

prediction.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin praedictiō, praedictiōnis; equivalent to predict + -ion. Compare the Germanic equivalents forespeaking, foretale, foretelling.

ex.en: Strange to say, his prediction has come true.
ex.ja: 不思議な話だが、彼の予言は当たった。

ex.en: To our surprise, her prediction came true.
ex.ja: 私たちが驚いたことに、彼女の予言が的中した。

ex.en: I'm afraid your prediction was wide of the mark.
ex.ja: 残念ながら、あなたの予測は的外れでした。

note.ja: pre（前もって）+ dict（言う）+ ion。前もって言うこと →「予言・予測」。

en: An experience of something in advance.
An advance showing of a film, exhibition etc.
To show or watch something, or part of it, before it is complete.
To show something in advance, a facility for viewing and checking a document or photo, or changes to it, before saving or printing it.

preview.ety: From pre- + view; compare Old French preveü, past participle of preveoir (“to foresee”).

ex.en: There was a special sneak preview last night.
ex.ja: 昨日の夜、特別試写会があった。

ex.en: My boss is out today, previewing the venue for the event.
ex.ja: 私の上司は今日はイベント会場の下見に出かけています。

note.ja: pre（前もって）+ view（見る）。「前もって見ること」→「下見・試写」。review（振り返って見る）と対。

en: The state of feeling confused or mystified because one cannot understand a complicated matter, a problem, etc.; bewilderment, confusion; …
A thing such as a complicated matter or a problem which is difficult to make sense of or understand; also, a person who is difficult to m…
To cause (oneself or someone, or their mind, etc.) to feel confused or mystified because they cannot understand a complicated matter, a p…
To use (one's brain or mind) to try to work out a complicated matter, a problem, etc.; also, to try to work out (a complicated matter, a …

puzzle.ety: The verb, of uncertain origin, is attested first. Apparently cognate with Scots pousle, pouzle, poozle (“to trifle; poke or potter around aimlessly; search about with uncertainty”), Saterland Frisian puzelje (“to work hard and continuously”), West Frisian peuzelje (“to trifle, work slowly; eat slowly and daintifully, snack”), Dutch peuzelen (“to perform insignificant work, dawdle; pick at, eat with relish in small pieces, snack”), German Low German pusseln (“to tinker, fiddle; trifle”) and pöseln (“to work hard, toil; to slave away; suffer at work; work slowly and ineffectively”), German posse

ex.en: I found it difficult to solve the puzzle.
ex.ja: そのパズルを解くのは難しかった。

ex.en: The solution of the puzzle required no time.
ex.ja: そのパズルを解くのに時間はかからなかった。

ex.en: I was puzzled about what to do next.
ex.ja: 私は次に何をやって良いのか途方に暮れた。

note.ja: 語源は不詳。16世紀ごろから「困らせる」→「難問・パズル」。

en: The knocker of a door.
A swinging knocker for making signals at the mouth of a shaft.
